Article Title: Captaincy weighed him down, freedom set him free: The remarkable second act of Joe Root
Article Text:
The remarkable act of Joe Root (Image: AI Generated)

India had no answer to Joe Root



Joe Root's bat drop celebration

'England's Greatest to Ever Play'



The many careers of Joe Root



JOE ROOT

'Captaincy Changed Root, But It Didn't Break Him'

Why Didn't Root Conquer T20 Cricket?

'Root is to England what Virat-Rohit are to India': Kumble

England's Answer to Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma



NEW DELHI: Joe Root finished the ODI series against India unbeaten, scoring 249 runs in three innings to guide England to a 2-1 series victory. At 36, while many of his contemporaries have retired, Root continues to redefine consistency across formats. All of Root's scores in this series 76, 99, and 74 came when the team needed him most, and he was deservedly named Player of the Series.Across the three-match ODI series against India, Root was England's batting backbone. He scored 76 in the first ODI to help England recover to 258 from 107/6, followed it up with a match-winning 99 in the second ODI while chasing 234, and finished with an unbeaten 74 in the third ODI, anchoring England's record 387-run total, supporting Ben Duckett's 141, and accelerating in the death overs.Joe Root breathed fire against India on his home soil and denied India a fairytale comeback after their 0-4 T20I series loss. In the presence of Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma , India fought well, but they could not stop the home hero, Root, who remained a headache for the visitors.Remember the bat-drop celebration by Root against India in 2018? That was the last time England won an ODI series against India, and the hero then was also none other than Root.He had scored 113* and 100 in that series and was named the Player of the Series.For over a decade, Root has been England's most dependable batter across Tests and ODIs, consistently delivering when the team needed him the most. Now 36, he continues to thrive despite many of his contemporaries, such as Alastair Cook, Eoin Morgan, Andrew Flintoff, Kevin Pietersen , and most recently Ben Stokes, having already retired from international cricket.The moot point is how Root continues to compete with youngsters the same way he did a decade ago. What is the secret behind his longevity? Former England spinner Monty Panesar, who once shared the dressing room with Root, revealed the secret.Speaking to TimesofIndia.com, Monty Panesar pointed out Root's hunger for runs and how he continues to evolve with every match, making every ground feel like his own den."I think he's simply hungry. He loves playing cricket and is still hungry to score runs. He still has that passion, and he probably wants to cement his status as one of England's greatest cricketers. With an ODI average above 50 and a Test average over 50, he probably feels he still has a few years left. When he retires, he wants to be remembered as England's greatest batter," Monty Panesar told TimesofIndia.com.In the modern T20 era, where batters look to come in, smash the ball, and walk away, Root prefers to stay at the crease and plays like an old-school batter who believes in building an innings rather than throwing away his wicket to a reckless shot."When I played with him, he had a very solid defence. He was always comfortable playing reverse sweeps, paddle sweeps, and those little scoring shots. He made them look very easy. You can see how his game has evolved, even in Test cricket, where he now plays the lap sweep over the slips for six. But on pitches like Cardiff, where there's extra bounce, you have to play a more traditional style of cricket. That's why his game is so effective. That's the difference between Joe Root and many of the younger players today," Monty Panesar added.There is another story that defines Joe Root's career – his journey before, during, and after captaincy.Before becoming captain (2012–January 2017), he scored 8,211 runs in 152 matches at an average of 48.58.During his Test captaincy (2017–April 2022), Root accumulated 8,680 runs in 149 matches at an average of 49.31.And since stepping down as captain in 2022, Root has enjoyed a remarkable resurgence. He has amassed 5,942 runs in 89 matches at an average of 53.05, scoring 20 centuries while rediscovering his best form in both Tests and ODIs."I think his captaincy period was extremely tough. England went through a difficult phase where they won only one of 17 Test matches, and eventually he had to step down. Those difficult moments probably made him stronger. Now he's enjoying the freedom that comes without the burden of captaincy, and he's making the most of it because he knows how hard things were during that period. I think those experiences have increased his hunger even further. He wants to continue playing for as long as possible because he's genuinely enjoying scoring runs for England again," Monty Panesar stated.Whenever Joe Root is compared with the Fab Four, one question is always asked: Why did he fail to dominate T20Is?There is Virat Kohli, who excelled in every format he played. Kane Williamson showcased his class across formats. Steve Smith did the same. But Root has always believed in elegant batting over power-hitting."I think his game is naturally more suited to the longer formats than T20 cricket, and that's probably why he hasn't been as successful in the shortest format. If you compare him with today's younger batters, their games are built around T20 cricket. Joe Root's strengths are more suited to Test cricket and ODIs. T20 is probably the hardest format for him because it demands explosive scoring and high-risk shots. On the other hand, his technique and temperament are perfectly suited to Test cricket and ODIs," Panesar explained.India have heavily relied on Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma for years. England, meanwhile, have relied on just one man whenever the batting has been under pressure: Joseph Edward Root. After Root's unbeaten 99 against India in the second ODI, former India captain Anil Kumble said: "What Virat and Rohit are for India, Root is for England."That statement perfectly justifies how far Root has come in his career."Joe Root gives someone like Harry Brook a lot of comfort. Harry Brook can go out there and play his attacking shots because he knows Joe Root is at the other end. When Root eventually retires, Brook may have to become more responsible, but right now Root allows the younger players to express themselves. The players know that if things become difficult, Joe Root is still there. It's similar to what Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma have meant for India," Monty Panesar said.That is probably the biggest compliment any batter can receive. When 10 other players and the coaching staff believe that, as long as you are at the crease, anything is possible, you know you have earned that respect. That is exactly what Root has built throughout his career.If Root goes on to break Sachin Tendulkar 's all-time Test run record, he needs only 1,807 more runs, wins another ICC title, and helps England reclaim the Ashes at home, there will be very little left for him to achieve in international cricket.As Panesar rightly pointed out: "If he does that, it would be the icing on the cake for Joe Root. Winning a World Cup in South Africa would be absolutely massive for him."For now, Root continues to do what he has done for more than a decade: score runs, frustrate bowlers, and prove that classical batting still has a place in the modern game.
Article Summary: Joe Root scored 249 runs in three innings to guide England to a 2-1 series victory. At 36, while many of his contemporaries have retired, Root continues to redefine consistency across formats. Former England spinner Monty Panesar, who once shared the dressing room with Root, revealed the secret.

Article Title: Asian Games 2026 Cricket Schedule: India, Pakistan on opposite sides of draw - full fixtures revealed
Article Text:
India's Richa Ghosh bats during the ICC Women's T20 World Cup, Group 1 cricket match between India and Pakistan in Birmingham, England. (Photo by AP/PTI)

Women's team to begin against Japan

The schedule for the cricket events at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, has been announced, with defending champions India receiving direct entry into the quarter-finals in both the men's and women's T20 tournaments.Cricket will be played in the T20 format and will have full international status. The women's competition will run from September 17 to 22, while the men's tournament will take place from September 24 to October 1 at Korogi Athletic Park in Aichi Prefecture.India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh have all been seeded into the men's quarter-finals based on their rankings. The remaining four quarter-final spots will be decided through a preliminary stage featuring six teams split into two groups.Group A includes Afghanistan, Japan and Nepal, while Group B features Hong Kong China, Malaysia and Oman.The top two teams from each group will qualify for the quarter-finals. Since India and Pakistan are on opposite sides of the draw, the two rivals can only meet if both reach the semi-finals or the final.India will face one of the teams that qualify from the preliminary round in the quarter-finals.India's women's team will start its title defence against hosts Japan in the quarter-finals. If India win, they will face either Bangladesh or China in the semi-finals.The other quarter-final matches will see Sri Lanka take on Malaysia, while Pakistan will play Thailand. India will be aiming to retain the gold medals won in both the men's and women's competitions at the Hangzhou Asian Games in 2023.
Article Summary: The schedule for the cricket events at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, has been announced. Defending champions India receive direct entry into the quarter-finals in both the men's and women's T20 tournaments. The women's competition will run from September 17 to 22. The men's tournament will take place from September 24 to October 1.

Article Title: The Hundred: New era, familiar result for London Spirit as Liam Livingstone heroics fall short
Article Text:
London Spirit captain Liam Livingstone scored a 40-ball 69 against Manchester Giants (ECB)

TimesofIndia.com in London:

New owners, new coaches, new players and a new captain. London Spirit arrived at Lord's on Thursday promising a fresh start, but their opening day of The Hundred 2026 produced a painfully familiar result.For the fifth time in six seasons, Spirit's men began their campaign with defeat as Manchester Super Giants edged a thriller by seven runs in front of 23,847 spectators. Earlier, Spirit's women had been comprehensively beaten by seven wickets, completing a double defeat for the hosts.In between came a distinctly Hundred-style interlude, with rapper Tinie Tempah performing amid jets of fire and even venturing into the Lord's crowd. But once attention returned to the cricket, it was Liam Livingstone who provided the evening's real entertainment.Spirit's new captain almost single-handedly dragged his side towards victory with an extraordinary all-round performance.Having put Manchester in, Spirit were initially made to toil by Tim Seifert, who marked his first Hundred appearance with 67 from 45 balls. The New Zealander added 49 with Jos Buttler (16) and 40 with Heinrich Klaasen (17) as the visitors reached 103 for two.That was when Livingstone took matters into his own hands.The captain bowled 20 of the final 25 deliveries, conceding only 14 runs and taking two wickets as Manchester spectacularly lost seven wickets for 35 runs. Six of those fell for just 22 runs in the final 26 balls, leaving the visitors on 138 for nine.On a Lord's surface where batters struggled for timing, only four days after England and India had combined for 747 runs in an ODI, Manchester's total appeared around par.Spirit's chase quickly ran into trouble when James Rew departed for a two-ball duck. Livingstone rebuilt alongside Kiran Carlson (19) before adding 68 with Dewald Brevis, although the South African's 22 came from 23 balls as the required rate climbed.With 56 needed from 30 balls, Livingstone shifted gears.He took 12 from Noor Ahmad's final five deliveries and brought up his half-century from 32 balls with a trademark slog sweep. Manchester also gave him a helping hand, most notably when Seifert spilled a chance at deep midwicket and watched the ball bounce over the boundary for six.Suddenly, Spirit were back in it.They required 21 from the final 10 deliveries, but Manchester's England pace duo held their nerve. Gus Atkinson removed Brevis with a caught-and-bowled dismissal and finished with figures of two for 15, leaving Sonny Baker to defend 12 from the final five balls.Baker had conceded 25 runs from his first 15 deliveries, while Livingstone had already struck five sixes.This time, however, the 23-year-old seamer won the battle. After conceding three runs from his first two deliveries, Baker went full and fast and crashed into Livingstone's stumps. James Coles was caught off the final ball as Spirit finished on 131 for six.Livingstone's 69 from 40 balls, coupled with figures of two for 14, earned him the Match Hero award but not the result."We bowled some really good stuff through the middle, dragged it back towards the end, and we nearly chased it down," Livingstone said. "We just got a bit too far behind the rate to catch up in the end."There was considerably less drama in the women's game.Grace Harris struck the opening delivery for four, but Spirit promptly collapsed to 23 for four in the powerplay and were eventually bowled out for 80 in 91 balls.Manchester needed only 59 deliveries to complete a seven-wicket win, with Paige Scholfield finishing the chase with successive four and six.For London Spirit, it was a sobering beginning to what was supposed to be a fresh chapter. Livingstone believes there is something to build on, and his own performance certainly provided encouragement.But for all the changes around Lord's, opening night brought the same old outcome: two games, two defeats.
Article Summary: London Spirit captain Liam Livingstone scored a 40-ball 69 against Manchester Giants (ECB) Livingstone's 69 from 40 balls earned him the Match Hero award but not the result. Spirit's women were comprehensively beaten by seven wickets, completing a double defeat.

Article Title: Chess legend Viswanathan Anand steps in as FIDE interim president after EU sanctions sideline Arkady Dvorkovich
Article Text:
Arkady Dvorkovich (on left) and Viswanathan Anand (PTI Photo)

AICF welcomes Anand's new role

India's Chess Olympiad squads announced

NEW DELHI: International Chess Federation (FIDE) President Arkady Dvorkovich has stepped aside from his role after being included in the European Union's latest sanctions list linked to Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine. The decision means FIDE Deputy President and former world champion Viswanathan Anand will serve as the interim president until the sanctions are lifted or overturned.In a statement released by FIDE, Dvorkovich described the sanctions as unjust and confirmed that he would challenge them through legal channels. However, he said his decision to temporarily suspend himself was taken to ensure the smooth functioning of the global governing body."Today, the EU decision to include my name in the 21st sanctions list was published. I want to state unequivocally that I consider this decision unlawful and unfair, and this decision will be immediately challenged by all possible means. I am confident that justice will prevail," FIDE's statement reads.He added that remaining in office while under sanctions could affect FIDE's day-to-day operations."However, given that until a formal court decision is rendered and/or such decision is cancelled or amended, these sanctions could hinder the stable functioning of FIDE, I have decided to voluntarily suspend the exercise of my powers and duties as FIDE President with immediate effect and for as long as I remain subject to sanctions under the EU and Swiss laws and regulations."Under Article 19.2 of the FIDE Charter, Anand will now take over as Interim President.The FIDE Council formally accepted Dvorkovich's decision and confirmed that he would not exercise any presidential powers or control over the federation or its assets while the sanctions remain in force.The FIDE presidential election at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand will go ahead as scheduled.The move was welcomed by All India Chess Federation (AICF) President Nitin Narang, who expressed confidence in Anand's leadership."As FIDE enters an interim phase of leadership, I extend my best wishes to Deputy President Viswanathan Anand as he assumes the responsibilities of Interim President," he wrote on X."Vishy sir has earned the respect of the global chess community through his integrity, wisdom and lifelong service to our sport. I am confident that under his stewardship, FIDE will continue to uphold stability, good governance and its commitment to players and federations across the world."The EU's 21st sanctions package targets 170 entities and 48 individuals with measures including possible asset freezes and travel bans. Despite the leadership change, FIDE said its activities, tournaments and social programmes will continue without interruption.Meanwhile, India has also announced its squads for the FIDE Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, to be held from September 17 to 27.Defending champions India will be led by reigning world champion D Gukesh, alongside R Praggnanandhaa, Arjun Erigaisi, Nihal Sarin and Vidit Gujrathi in the open section, while Koneru Humpy headlines the women's team with R Vaishali, Divya Deshmukh, Vantika Agrawal and Savitha Shri B.
Article Summary: International Chess Federation (FIDE) President Arkady Dvorkovich has stepped aside from his role after being included in the European Union's latest sanctions list linked to Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine. FIDE Deputy President and former world champion Viswanathan Anand will serve as the interim president until the sanctions are lifted or overturned.

Article Title: From doubt to dominance: Jadumani Singh's career-changing move to 55kg fuels CWG dream
Article Text:
Jadumani Singh Mandengbam from India in red (Photo by Getty Images)

When Jadumani Singh decided to move up from 50kg to the 55kg category, there were plenty of doubters. Many believed the Manipuri boxer, shorter than most of his rivals in the division, would struggle against bigger opponents.Some even warned that the move could derail the momentum he had built after capping an impressive 2025 season with a silver medal at the World Boxing Cup Finals in the men's 50kg.The 23-year-old from Iroishemba in Manipur, however, chose to block out the noise.Months later, the gamble paid off. Jadumani not only won the national title in his new weight class and was adjudged the Best Boxer of the tournament, but also secured place in India’s squads for the Commonwealth Games and the Asian Games “People kept saying I wouldn’t be able to do well in 55kg because of my height. At times, it affected me mentally, but deep down I believed I could succeed,” said Jadumani, who will begin his CWG campaign against Scotland’s Aaron Cullen in the men’s 55kg Round of 32 on Friday.The move was driven by a bigger ambition. With the 51kg category no longer part of Los Angeles Olympics programme and his long-term target being an Olympic medal, Jadumani realised he had to think beyond immediate success.Before taking the plunge, he spent hours discussing the decision with former world champion L. Sarita Devi , who has remained one of his biggest mentors even after he joined the Army Sports Institute (ASI) in Pune.“That decision to move to 55kg became the biggest turning point of his career. Self-belief is the most important thing. I first asked him if he truly believed he could succeed in the new category. When he said yes, I told him I would support him completely,” Sarita said.The transition was anything but easy. Every bout at the National Championships tested him. Jadumani defeated several established names, including former Commonwealth Games champion Amit Panghal , before clinching the title and the Best Boxer award.“I didn’t pay attention to what anyone was saying. I just focused on my boxing. My only aim was to become champion,” he said.The national title proved to be the launchpad for an impressive run. Jadumani claimed bronze at Boxam Elite International in Spain, pushed top seed Rui Yamaguchi in a closely fought contest at the Asian Championships before bouncing back with gold at Grand Prix Usti Nad Labem in Czechia. He then topped the national trials to seal his place in India’s squads for the CWG and Asiad.The self-belief that carried him through the toughest phase of his career has been with him since he first stepped into a boxing ring. Introduced to the sport by his uncle, Mandengbam Milan Singh, Jadumani initially knew little about boxing.“My uncle wanted me to take up an individual sport. Everyone in the family played football, but he felt I would have a better future in boxing,” he said.Sarita’s influence, meanwhile, has extended far beyond technical guidance.“She has taught me discipline and the importance of maintaining my diet. Before every major competition, we speak over a video call. Whenever I feel low, she motivates me and helps me stay focused,” he said.As he prepares to make his Commonwealth Games debut in Glasgow, Jadumani believes the sacrifices have all been worthwhile. Last year, he managed to spend barely 15 to 20 days at home as he trained relentlessly to establish himself in the new weight category.Sarita believes the sacrifices will eventually bear fruit.“An athlete only needs one opportunity. Jadumani got that opportunity, proved himself, and I believe he has what it takes to win medals for India on the biggest stage,” she said with pride before signing off.
Article Summary: Jadumani Singh will make his Commonwealth Games debut on Friday. The 23-year-old moved up from 50kg to the 55kg category last year. He won the national title in his new weight class and was adjudged the Best Boxer of the tournament.

Article Title: Durand Cup set to introduce women's tournament from next edition
Article Text:
Durand Cup Trophy tour concludes in Kolkata ahead of tournament opener (ANI Photo)

Kolkata: The oldest football tournament in Asia — Durand Cup — will host its 135th edition when Mohun Bagan Super Giant and East Bengal FC take the field at Salt Lake Stadium in the first derby of the season on Saturday.However, in the 134 years of the tournament’s existence, Indian women’s football has grown by leaps and bounds, and at the culmination of Durand Cup Trophy Tour in the city on Wednesday, the organisers of the prestigious competition — the Indian Armed Forces — revealed their enthusiasm to include a women’s competition in the coming years.At the ceremonial function and news conference at AOI Vijay Durg, where the tournament’s three iconic trophies were showcased, Major General Dinesh Kumar Singh, vice-chairman of Durand Cup Organising Committee, said they were mulling the introduction of a women’s tournament alongside the men’s event in the near future."Why leave the girls behind?" was the question on their minds six months ago when they began preparations for the upcoming season, Singh said.“So, this is something that we have already thought about. The issue is how many venues and what kind of facilities (will be available) for it. So probably in the next edition we may have a truncated or a smaller version of the girls’ event,” he added.To add to the expectations, a special women's exhibition match was organised jointly by the Indian Armed Forces and the govt of Manipur at the SAI Ground in Takyel, Imphal, in the build-up to the main competition.This time, the tournament will see 24 men’s teams compete across five venues, with Ranchi as the newest addition and the Assam matches returning to Guwahati after two editions in Kokrajhar.“We saw the enthusiasm among the people in Kokrajhar. But the state government wanted it back in Guwahati for ease of organisation,” said Lieutenant General Gambhir Singh, Chief of Staff, Headquarters Eastern Command, and chairman of the Organising Committee.Among the dignitaries at the event was chief guest Dr Indranil Khan, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for the Departments of Youth Services and Sports and Consumer Affairs in the West Bengal government.“During the recent FIFA World Cup , we all supported clubs from around the world. Now it is time to unite behind Indian football and our own footballers,” said Khan.Meanwhile, Ranchi will host its first-ever Durand Cup match on Sunday, when Jamshedpur FC take on Defenders FC at Birsa Munda Stadium. Defending champions NorthEast United FC will begin their title defence against Bodoland FC at Guwahati’s Indira Gandhi Athletic Stadium on Aug 1. The other cities hosting the premier competition are the football-crazy northeastern cities of Shillong and Imphal.
Article Summary: Mohun Bagan Super Giant and East Bengal FC take the field at Salt Lake Stadium on Saturday. Ranchi will host its first-ever Durand Cup match on Sunday, when Jamshedpur FC take on Defenders FC at Birsa Munda Stadium. Defending champions NorthEast United FC will begin their title defence against Bodoland FC at Guwahati’s Indira Gandhi Athletic Stadium on Aug 1.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Indian boxers unfazed by baggage snag on arrival
Article Text:
Santiago Nieva (Image credit: X)

India’s boxing contingent arrived in Glasgow confident after a productive two-week multinational training camp in Belfast, but its final preparations were briefly disrupted when some boxers’ luggage failed to arrive ahead of Thursday’s opening ceremony.The 14-member squad travelled from Belfast to Glasgow on Tuesday after completing the intensive camp, during which the boxers benefitted from quality sparring and competition-specific training. However, several athletes were left without their bags, which also contained their ceremonial outfits, TOI has learnt.Sources said officials from the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and the chef-de-mission’s office were at the airport on Wednesday, coordinating with the airline to ensure the baggage reached the contingent before the ceremony. The boxing competition begins on Friday and runs until Aug 1.The incident, however, has not gone down well with the Boxing Federation of India (BFI). Sources said that after the issue surfaced, the federation asked the boxers to submit declarations stating that they would not speak to the media about internal team matters and would instead remain focused on their performances.Despite the logistical hiccup, the mood in the camp remains upbeat. “We are settling in well in Glasgow. We had a good camp in Belfast where everybody got quality sparring and proper preparations. The boxers are managing their weights well. We will have the draws soon. We are coming with high expectations for this competition,” India women’s head coach Santiago Nieva told TOI .India’s 14-member squad features Olympic bronze medallist Lovlina Borgohain and Jaismine Lamboria, the world No. 1 in the women’s 57kg category.
Article Summary: India’s boxing contingent arrived in Glasgow confident after a productive two- week multinational training camp in Belfast. The 14-member squad travelled from Belfast to Glasgow on Tuesday after completing the intensive camp. Several athletes were left without their bags, which also contained their ceremonial outfits, TOI has learnt.

Article Title: 'Not up to the standard': Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza blames pitch for India defeat
Article Text:
Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza on the right (ANI Photo)

Positives despite the defeat

Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza blamed the pitch after his team's seven-wicket loss to India in the opening T20I of the three-match series at the Harare Sports Club.Raza said the surface had too much moisture early on, making batting difficult with the new ball, while conditions became much easier when India came out to chase. India comfortably chased 126 in 13.2 overs, powered by Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's record-breaking 18-ball half-century to take a 1-0 lead in the series.Raza felt the pitch favoured the team batting second and said Zimbabwe struggled because the ball continued to move for longer than expected."Again, not up to the standard, I think. In the morning, I think that moisture certainly played a part, but I didn't think it was going to play a part for that long. I thought it remained tough with the new ball," Raza said after the match."Unfortunately, we didn't hit many boundaries up front as well, so the ball stayed new, and because of that, I felt the movement off the deck made batting even tougher," he added.Comparing it with the recent Bangladesh ODI series, Raza said the wicket became much better to bat on during India's innings."I thought during the Bangladesh ODI series, there was a lot of moisture, and it remained there for a long time.Whereas today, I thought the moisture was there for the first eight to ten or even 12 overs, and apart from that, when India came out to bat, the wicket was very true," he said.Zimbabwe recovered from 32/4 to post 125/7, thanks to Wessly Madhevere and Tadiwanashe Marumani. Raza praised the pair for helping the team reach a respectable total and hoped the rest of the batting unit would contribute more in the coming matches."So, hopefully, we get a better wicket for the next game so that even when we lose the toss, it doesn't play too big a part," he added."Yes, definitely. That's one of the positives. Marumani and Madhevere, it's a new role as well. I thought they batted really well to give us some sort of a respectable total. We'll take that as a positive, and hopefully the other guys can chip in as well so that we can put up a competitive total if we bat first," he said.
Article Summary: Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza blamed the pitch after his team's seven-wicket loss to India in the opening T20I of the three-match series. India comfortably chased 126 in 13.2 overs, powered by Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's record-breaking 18-ball half-century to take a 1-0 lead in the series.

Article Title: Injuries denied her twice: Sakshi Chaudhary is finally ready for the Commonwealth Games
Article Text:
India's Sakshi Chaudhary (PTI Photo)

New Delhi :

In Haryana’s boxing heartland of Bhiwani, dreams are often forged inside crowded rings filled with aspiring boxers before blossoming on the world stage. Sakshi Chaudhary , a product of the famed Bhiwani Boxing Club, has travelled that familiar road, but not without heartbreak. Shoulder injuries robbed the 25-year-old of a place at the 2022 Birmingham Commonwealth Games and the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games . Four years later, she finally gets her chance.When India’s boxing campaign begins at the Glasgow CWG, Sakshi will enter the ring as one of the country’s leading medal prospects. The women’s 51kg boxer opens her campaign against Botswana’s Lethabo Modukanele on July 27, carrying not just the nation’s hopes but also the weight of opportunities once lost.“The India jersey always motivates me to fight for gold. I had been waiting for this opportunity. After missing the CWG and Asian Games earlier because of injuries, I’m finally here. My preparations have been very good. I’ve sharpened my technique and attacking game, and my height and reach will be an advantage,” Sakshi told TOI .The boxer from Dhanana village, whose father is a farmer and mother a homemaker, credits legendary coach Jagdish Singh with shaping her career before she joined the Army. Her road to Glasgow required reinvention. A natural 54kg boxer, Sakshi dropped down to 51kg after Preeti Pawar secured India’s 54kg berth by winning gold at the Asian Championships.She shed nearly three kilograms in three weeks and justified the gamble, defeating Jyoti Gulia, former world champion Nikhat Zareen and reigning world champion Minakshi Hooda during the selection trials at NIS Patiala in May.“This was a do-or-die situation for me. I wanted to go all out because qualifying for the CWG and Asian Games meant everything after losing out previously,” she said.The move has also suited her boxing. “In 54kg, many boxers come down from higher weights and there’s more power. In 51kg, my height advantage helps me much more.”A two-time World youth champion, World junior champion and Asian Championships medallist, Sakshi is now making a smooth transition to senior boxing. For the boxer who once watched two major Games slip away, Glasgow offers the chance to script the comeback she has long imagined.Stay Updated With: CWG Schedule 2026
Article Summary: Sakshi Chaudhary is a product of the famed Bhiwani Boxing Club. The 25-year-old missed the 2022 Birmingham Commonwealth Games and the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games due to injuries. Sakshi dropped to 51kg after Preeti Pawar secured India’s 54kg berth by winning gold at the Asian Championships.

Article Title: 'Where is Rajat Patidar?' - Former India batter questions selectors over Zimbabwe T20I squad
Article Text:
Rajat Patidar with the IPL trophy (ANI Photo)

Vihari questions squad balance

Vihari also backs Kuldeep and Samson

Former India batter Hanuma Vihari has criticised the Indian team management for leaving Rajat Patidar out of India's T20I squad for the Zimbabwe series.Vihari believes Patidar deserved a place after his impressive performances and leadership with Royal Challengers Bengaluru, while also questioning the overall balance of the squad.India, however, made a strong start to the series by defeating Zimbabwe by seven wickets in the opening T20I at the Harare Sports Club on Thursday to take a 1-0 lead in the three-match contest.After restricting Zimbabwe to 125/7, India chased down the target in just 13.2 overs, thanks to a sensational half-century from 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who became the youngest player to score a fifty in men's international cricket.His 18-ball fifty included four fours and four sixes.Earlier, Mayank Yadav (2/18) and Prince Yadav (2/19) starred with the ball, while India also named role-specific concussion substitutes for the first time, including Suryansh Shedge, Prabhsimran Singh, Harsh Dubey and Yash Thakur.Vihari said the selectors made some difficult decisions, especially by leaving out Patidar despite the squad featuring several left-handed batters. He felt a right-handed batter like Patidar or Sanju Samson would have given the team better balance."Rinku Singh was brought back, but where is Rajat Patidar? He led RCB to titles in two seasons and also performed well as a batter. He was not considered as well. These are hard calls from the selectors. Patidar should have been given a chance, especially because if you look at the team, all are left-handers. With so many left-handers, Patidar or Samson as right-handers should have been there. Yes, Prabhsimran is there, but I don't think he will play because Ishan Kishan will be the first choice wicketkeeper," Vihari said on his YouTube channel.Vihari also questioned the omission of experienced wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav and wicketkeeper-batter Sanju Samson. He pointed out that Patidar scored 486 runs at a strike rate of 196.76 in IPL 2026 and felt performances should matter more than age while picking the squad."It's a serious case of why Kuldeep Yadav has not been included. He is a wrist-spinner with experience. Why did you not play him? Also, if you did not want Sanju Samson for the Zimbabwe series, you sent Prabhsimran. Fine. But you did not even consider giving an opportunity to Rajat Patidar. Why should age be a factor?" Vihari asked."If you have taken many players who performed in the IPL, then why not Patidar? You have filled the team with left-handers. There is no right-hander apart from Shreyas," he added.
Article Summary: Rajat Patidar left out of India's T20I squad for the Zimbabwe series. Former India batter Hanuma Vihari questions squad balance. India beat Zimbabwe by seven wickets to take 1-0 lead in three-match series.

Article Title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's maiden T20I fifty seals emphatic India victory
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (ANI Photo)

Showing the kind of murderous touch that has made him the most feared batsman in the IPL, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi blazed to his maiden international half-century as India thrashed Zimbabwe by seven wickets, with 40 balls to spare, in the opening T20I at the Harare Sports Club on Thursday.Aged 15 years and 118 days, Sooryavanshi smashed 50 off only 18 balls in an innings studded with four sixes and four fours.The teenage batting sensation had endured a difficult start to his international career during India's T20I series against England in July, after scores of 14 (10), 13 (5) and 15 (10) in his first three innings.Returning to the scene of his 80-ball 175 against England in the 2026 U-19 World Cup final, the precociously talented opener produced a dazzling display to make light work of a modest 126-run chase, racing to an 18-ball fifty.Sooryavanshi smashed 19 runs off Richard Ngarava in the second over, clobbering the left-arm pacer for two sixes.Zimbabwe hit back in the third over as Blessing Muzarabani (2-26) had Abhishek Sharma , who scratched around for one off eight balls, caught at deep backward point off a slash. But Sooryavanshi continued to attack, launching two more sixes straight down the ground besides several fiercely struck boundaries.He eventually fell to Ngarava in the seventh over, chasing a wide delivery outside off and top-edging to Ben Curran at deep third.By then, however, India had raced to 68 and the youngster had virtually settled the contest.The visitors completed the chase in just 13.2 overs. The win also ended new T20 captain Shreyas Iyer 's winless run, as he registered his maiden victory in his eighth match in charge. Shreyas had lost six of his first seven games as captain during the tours of Ireland and England.It was also India's first win to kick off the three-match series since lifting the 2026 T20 World Cup in March.Earlier, India's new-look pace attack starred after the visitors elected to field, with Mayank Yadav (2-18) and Prince Yadav (2-19) sharing four wickets for just 37 runs in eight overs to restrict Zimbabwe to 125 for seven.Vindicating the selectors' decision to back him despite an ordinary IPL 2026, Mayank made an immediate impact by dismissing opener Brian Bennett, who had scored 97 against India in the 2026 T20 World Cup in Chennai, with the very first ball of the match.His 150 kmph thunderbolt brushed Bennett's bat before carrying through to wicketkeeper Ishan Kishan, whose review overturned the umpire's decision. Mayank struck again in the fifth over, removing No. 3 batter Dion Myers for six, caught at mid-on.Prince accounted for the other opener, debutant Ben Curran, as Zimbabwe slumped to 20 for three. The hosts slipped further to 32 for four in the eighth over when captain Sikandar Raza (4) pulled Shivam Dube straight to substitute fielder Suryansh Shedge at deep midwicket.Brief scores: India 126 for 3 (Sooryavanshi 50, Kishan 35, Muzarabani 2-26) beat Zimbabwe 125 for 7 (Madhevere 39, Mayank 2-18, Prince 2-19) by seven wickets.
Article Summary: India beat Zimbabwe by seven wickets in the opening T20I at Harare Sports Club. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi smashed 50 off only 18 balls in an innings studded with four sixes and four fours. India completed the chase in just 13.2 overs.

Article Title: 'My dream has come true': Emotional Ashok Sharma dedicates India debut to elder brother Akshay
Article Text:
Ashok Sharma getting his India cap from Sunil Joshi. (Pic credit: BCCI)

A brother's sacrifice that changed everything



India's Ashok Sharma bowls as Zimbabwe's batsman Dion Myers watches on. (AP Photo)

Laxman's special message before debut



From IPL pace sensation to India colours



NEW DELHI: India fast bowler Ashok Sharma described his international debut as a "dream come true" after receiving his maiden India cap ahead of the opening T20I against Zimbabwe in Harare on Thursday, dedicating the emotional milestone to his elder brother whose sacrifice helped shape his cricketing journey.The 24-year-old Rajasthan pacer was handed his India cap by bowling coach Sunil Joshi before the toss, capping a remarkable rise from domestic cricket to the international stage. Although Ashok finished with figures of 0/29 in four overs, India secured a comfortable seven-wicket victory to take a 1-0 lead in the three-match series.Overcome with emotion after the cap presentation, Ashok reflected on years of hard work finally paying off."It's very special. The thing for which I was working hard, hopefully today it's fulfilled. It's a dream. Till now it's a dream, sir, whatever it was. Even now it's a dream that I wore the cap of India, and my dream has come true," he said.The young pacer then revealed the person he wanted to honour the most."I dedicate this moment to my elder brother," he added.Ashok's story is one of perseverance and family sacrifice.Growing up in Rampura, a small village near Jaipur, he shared a passion for cricket with his elder brother, Akshay Sharma, who also played the game.However, financial constraints meant the family could not afford to support both sons in pursuing cricket.Akshay made the difficult decision to put aside his own ambitions so Ashok could attend inter-district Under-16 trials. That selfless act became the turning point in Ashok's career.Years later, the youngster who once struggled for opportunities has now become India's newest fast-bowling prospect.Before presenting the India cap, stand-in head coach VVS Laxman reminded Ashok of the significance of representing the country."We know Ashok is going to make his international debut, and we discussed that it's a matter of great honour," he said.Laxman also acknowledged the effort behind the achievement."Representing the country, all your hard work, and all your performances were rewarded by this opportunity," he added.Ashok's rise has been rapid over the past year.After finishing as the leading wicket-taker in the 2025-26 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy with 22 wickets, he earned an IPL contract with Gujarat Titans, where he grabbed headlines by clocking 154.2 kmph — the fastest delivery of IPL 2026.Earlier in his journey, he almost walked away from cricket before a chance appearance at the Red Bull Speedster competition opened the doors to becoming a Rajasthan Royals net bowler, eventually paving the way for his domestic breakthrough.Though he went wicketless on debut against Zimbabwe, Ashok consistently hit a lively pace and showcased the attributes that earned him national selection.
Article Summary: Ashok Sharma receives his India cap ahead of the opening T20I against Zimbabwe. The 24-year-old Rajasthan pacer was handed his cap by bowling coach Sunil Joshi. India secured a comfortable seven-wicket victory to take a 1-0 lead in the three-match series.

Article Title: LPL 2026: Jaffna Kings terminated mid-season after co-owner's arrest and corruption allegations
Article Text:
Jaffna Kings franchise agreement terminated (Image: X)

Why Was the Franchise Terminated?



IPG assures stability



The Jaffna Kings will continue their Lanka Premier League (LPL) 2026 campaign despite their franchise rights being terminated by Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) and tournament organiser Innovative Production Group (IPG) over financial and contractual breaches. The decision, announced on Thursday, sees all franchise rights revert to IPG, which, alongside SLC, has assumed complete operational control of the four-time champions to ensure the tournament proceeds without disruption.According to SLC and IPG, the franchise owners failed to fulfil their financial obligations under the franchise agreement. The termination comes in the middle of the tournament following a series of controversies surrounding the ownership group, Sports Commune.Co-owner Manjot Kalra was arrested over corruption-related allegations, while another owner, Mayank Goel, has become unreachable. The ownership group also allegedly failed to pay player and staff salaries and mismanaged sponsor funds, leading to the cancellation of the franchise agreement.As a result, IPG and SLC have taken direct control of the team's operations. Despite the ownership shake-up, the Jaffna Kings will continue under the same name with their existing squad, coaching staff and support personnel.IPG CEO Anil Mohan stressed that safeguarding the tournament's integrity remained the organisers' top priority."While this was a difficult decision, our priority has always been to protect the integrity of the Lanka Premier League and ensure complete stability for our players, coaches, partners and fans. Together with Sri Lanka Cricket, we have acted swiftly to ensure the Jaffna Kings continue to participate in the tournament without disruption. We want to assure everyone that all operational matters, including player contracts, staff commitments and team logistics, are being managed seamlessly. The sixth edition of the LPL will proceed as planned, and we remain fully committed to delivering another successful and world-class tournament," Anil Mohan said.On the field, the Bhanuka Rajapaksa-led Jaffna Kings have made a positive start to their campaign, winning two of their first three matches. The sixth edition of the Lanka Premier League began on July 17 and is scheduled to conclude on August 8.
Article Summary: Jaffna Kings franchise rights terminated by Sri Lanka Cricket and tournament organiser Innovative Production Group (IPG) Decision comes in the middle of the tournament following a series of controversies surrounding the ownership group, Sports Commune. Co-owner Manjot Kalra was arrested over corruption-related allegations, while another owner, Mayank Goel, has become unreachable.

Article Title: 'He is fearless': Shreyas Iyer hails Vaibhav Sooryavanshi after record-breaking blitz vs Zimbabwe
Article Text:
Captain Shreyas Iyer and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (Pic credit: BCCI)

A perfect response after a quiet England tour



ALSO READ:

Iyer celebrates first win as India captain



NEW DELHI: India captain Shreyas Iyer reserved special praise for teenage batting prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi after the 15-year-old produced a breathtaking match-winning knock to power India to a seven-wicket victory over Zimbabwe in the opening T20I in Harare on Thursday.Sooryavanshi smashed 50 off just 19 balls, bringing up his maiden international half-century in only 18 deliveries as India chased down 126 in just 13.2 overs. The left-hander's explosive innings also saw him become the youngest player in men's international cricket to score a fifty, eclipsing a record previously held by Nepal's Kushal Malla.Following the emphatic victory, Iyer was full of admiration for the teenager's fearless approach."He is fearless, the way he approaches the innings is amazing. He possesses immense confidence when he steps onto the field," Iyer said after registering his first victory as India's T20I captain.Sooryavanshi's international career had begun quietly earlier this month during India's tour of England, where scores of 14, 13 and 15 saw him dropped for the final T20I as India lost the series.However, a return to the Harare Sports Club — where he had blasted 175 off just 80 balls in the Under-19 World Cup final earlier this year — proved to be the perfect stage for the youngster to announce himself.After taking four deliveries to settle in, Sooryavanshi launched a stunning counterattack. He hammered four boundaries and four towering sixes, dismantling Zimbabwe's bowling attack with a fearless display of strokeplay.His innings effectively ended the contest inside the Powerplay before Richard Ngarava eventually dismissed him one ball after he reached his half-century. Ishan Kishan (35) and captain Iyer (28 not out) then completed the chase with ease.The victory also marked a significant personal milestone for Iyer, who finally tasted success after enduring a difficult start to his tenure as India's T20I captain.Having lost all seven of his previous matches in charge during tours of Ireland and England, the 31-year-old celebrated his maiden win as skipper in style.Iyer praised both his bowlers and batters for executing the team's plans perfectly."Exceptional. They were tremendous in their execution. Can't be more happier to get my first win," he said.The captain also explained his decision to bowl first after winning the toss."I was anticipating the bounce and there was a decent amount of bounce. Exceptional start given by Mayank. Didn't give them room," he said.Mayank Yadav set the tone by dismissing Brian Bennett with the very first ball of the match before finishing with two wickets, while Prince Yadav also claimed two scalps as Zimbabwe were restricted to 125 for seven. India then made light work of the chase thanks largely to Sooryavanshi's stunning assault.
Article Summary: India beat Zimbabwe by seven wickets in the opening T20I in Harare. Teenage batsman Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scored 50 off just 19 balls. He became the youngest player in men's international cricket to score a fifty.

Article Title: 'Mental strength makes a huge difference': Mayank Yadav reflects on comeback after 21-month
Article Text:
Mayank Yadav

India fast bowler Mayank Yadav said improving mentally and understanding his body better during rehabilitation helped him make a successful return after a 21-month injury layoff.Back in India's colours after nearly two years, Mayank returned figures of 2/18 in four overs as India restricted Zimbabwe to 125/7 in the opening T20I of the three-match series at the Harare Sports Club on Thursday.The pacer, who underwent surgery for a stress fracture in his back in Christchurch, New Zealand, in July 2025, made an immediate impact by dismissing Brian Bennett with the very first ball of the innings. Bowling consistently above 140 kmph, he extracted seam movement and bounce to trouble Zimbabwe's batters throughout his spell."It's always a great feeling when you come back and play for your country and especially bowl like this, this type of spell. It's a fantastic feeling, and I don't think I can describe it well through my words."Obviously it was there because I was coming after two years and there is always pressure when you come to play for your country.So, I was a little bit nervous. But my thinking and my plan was very simple to just execute my strength and just keep bowling," Mayank said during a mid-innings interview with the broadcasters.He added that the early wicket helped him settle quickly."Definitely after the first ball wicket I calmed down a lot. I got confidence. I'm playing after a while, but still I can deliver with the skills I have, that strength I have; it will help me a lot on these types of wickets, especially."Reflecting on his recovery, Mayank said the biggest change came mentally rather than physically."There are a lot of things: physical training, mentally. When you're injured and, in that phase, mental strength makes a huge difference for any player."So, I think more than physically, for me, mentally I got much better, and I knew my body a lot after the surgery and after the rehab. So, it makes a huge difference for me," he concluded.India completed a comfortable seven-wicket victory, thanks largely to Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's explosive half-century. The teenager raced to a fifty in just 18 balls, his first substantial innings in international cricket, scoring 50 off 19 deliveries with four fours and four sixes.After Mayank and the bowlers restricted Zimbabwe to 125/7, India chased down the target in 13.2 overs to take a 1-0 lead in the three-match series.
Article Summary: India fast bowler Mayank Yadav made a successful return after a 21-month injury layoff. Mayank returned figures of 2/18 in four overs as India restricted Zimbabwe to 125/7 in the opening T20I of the three-match series. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi raced to a fifty in just 18 balls, his first substantial innings in international cricket.

Article Title: IND vs ZIM, 1st T20I: Captain Shreyas Iyer ends seven-match winless streak as India crush Zimbabwe by 7 wickets
Article Text:
Shreyas Iyer registers first win in Harare (Image: X/BCCI)

Mayank Yadav shines on comeback



Sooryavanshi rewrites history



India finally ended their seven-match winless run under captain Shreyas Iyer , defeating Zimbabwe by seven wickets in the first T20I at Harare on Thursday. The match also witnessed teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi script history by becoming the youngest player to score a T20I half-century.After winning the toss, Iyer opted to bowl first, and India's pace attack justified the decision with a clinical performance.Returning to international cricket for the first time since October 2024 after recovering from a stress fracture, Mayank Yadav made an immediate impact. The express pacer dismissed Brian Bennett with the very first ball of the match before removing Dion Myers, consistently clocking speeds in excess of 145 kmph.Zimbabwe were reduced to 26/3 inside the powerplay and slipped further to 32/4 after Shivam Dube dismissed captain Sikandar Raza.A fighting partnership between Wessly Madhevere (39) and Ryan Burl (26), along with an unbeaten 27 off 20 from Tadiwanashe Marumani, helped the hosts recover to 125/7 in their allotted 20 overs. Debutant Ashok Sharma recovered well after an expensive first over, while Ravi Bishnoi bowled economically to finish with 1/24.Chasing 126, India suffered an early setback when Abhishek Sharma was dismissed for just 1. However, it proved to be Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's day.The 15-year-old prodigy unleashed a breathtaking assault, smashing 50 off just 19 balls with four fours and four sixes. In the process, he became the youngest player ever to score a T20I half-century, putting India firmly in control of the chase before falling immediately after reaching his milestone.Captain Shreyas Iyer anchored the innings with an unbeaten 28 off 24 balls, while Ishan Kishan chipped in with a quick 35 off 24. Tilak Varma struck the winning runs as India completed the chase comfortably with seven wickets in hand.For Zimbabwe, Blessing Muzarabani was the pick of the bowlers with two wickets, dismissing Abhishek Sharma and Ishan Kishan, while Richard Ngarava claimed the prized scalp of Sooryavanshi.The victory marked Shreyas Iyer's first win as India's T20I captain, ending a frustrating seven-match winless streak that included the tours of Ireland and England, while Sooryavanshi's record-breaking knock stole the headlines in Harare.
Article Summary: India beat Zimbabwe by seven wickets in the first T20I at Harare. Teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi becomes youngest player to score a T 20I half- century. Mayank Yadav makes an immediate impact after returning to international cricket.

Article Title: Watch: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's emotional 'A' celebration steals hearts after historic world-record fifty
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (Pic credit: BCCI)

WATCH:

The emotional story behind the viral celebration



World record at just 15 years and 118 days



NEW DELHI: India's teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi once again captured the spotlight on Thursday — not just for rewriting cricket history, but also for the heartfelt celebration that followed his record-breaking half-century.The 15-year-old produced a breathtaking innings against Zimbabwe in the first T20I at Harare, smashing a 50 off just 18 balls to become the youngest player ever to score a fifty in men's international cricket.Moments after reaching the milestone, Sooryavanshi broke into his now-famous 'A' celebration, forming the letter with his fingers before acknowledging the dressing room. The emotional gesture, which first went viral during IPL 2026, has now become synonymous with the young opener.The left-hander's explosive knock featured four boundaries and four sixes, giving India a flying start in their chase of 126 after Zimbabwe were restricted to 125/7.While the celebration sparked widespread curiosity during the IPL, Sooryavanshi had initially played down its significance, insisting he simply enjoyed trying different celebrations after reaching milestones."I don't know. I just do something new every match. I don't really plan it.There's no meaning behind it," he had said after one of his IPL knocks.However, the real meaning behind the gesture later emerged in a behind-the-scenes Rajasthan Royals video.Speaking to team manager Romi Bhinder, the youngster finally revealed that the 'A' is a tribute to his mother, Aarti."The celebration is for my mother. Her name starts with the letter 'A'," Sooryavanshi had revealed.Since then, the celebration has become his trademark, and Thursday's emotional tribute carried even greater significance after he etched his name into the record books.At 15 years and 118 days, Sooryavanshi eclipsed Nepal's Kushal Malla, who previously held the record after scoring his maiden international fifty at 15 years and 340 days.The Indian opener also surpassed some of cricket's biggest names on the all-time list. Sachin Tendulkar scored his maiden international fifty at 16 years and 213 days in a Test against Pakistan in 1989, while Shahid Afridi reached the milestone at 16 years and 214 days during an ODI against Sri Lanka in 1996.The innings also made Sooryavanshi the youngest player ever to register a 50-plus score in men's T20Is, comfortably bettering Gibraltar's Louis Bruce, who had held the previous T20I age record.Already one of the biggest stories of IPL 2026, Sooryavanshi has now carried that form onto the international stage.
Article Summary: India's Vaibhav Sooryavanshi becomes youngest player ever to score a 50 in men's international cricket. The 15-year-old smashes a 50 off just 18 balls against Zimbabwe in the first T20I at Harare. He broke into his now-famous 'A' celebration, forming the letter with his fingers before acknowledging the dressing room. The emotional gesture first went viral during IPL 2026 and has now become synonymous with the young opener.

Article Title: After selling e-rickshaw to fund his dream, Jhandu eyes CWG medal
Article Text:
Bihar’s Jhandu Kumar

In 2021, during the Covid-19 pandemic, Bihar’s Jhandu Kumar drove an e-rickshaw to earn a living and support his family after he was forced to temporarily shut down the family-run vegetable shop at Harnaut Bazaar in Nalanda district due to the construction of an overbridge.It was a major setback to his sporting ambitions.Until then, despite financial struggles and being affected by polio from the age of five, he had managed to keep his dream alive by winning medals at state and national competitions in both para and able-bodied powerlifting.“Every day I used to travel nearly 20km to Bihar Sharif to buy vegetables, bring them back and sell them in the market. After finishing work around 4 pm, I would go to the gym for training,” Jhandu told TOI from Glasgow, where he will compete in the men’s heavyweight category of para-powerlifting on Friday.He followed that routine every day while training under Gautam Singh at Rockstar Gym. However, the money he earned was rarely enough to meet the demands of his diet.“I was earning only around ₹400-500 a day through my business, while protein supplements alone would cost nearly ₹1,000. Managing my diet and training was a huge challenge,” recalled the 29-year-old.Things became even more difficult after he started driving the e-rickshaw.Although it provided a steady income, the long hours left him too exhausted to train properly. Once the family was able to reopen the vegetable shop, he made another sacrifice to keep his sporting dream alive.“I sold my e-rickshaw in 2023 to participate in the National Para Powerlifting Championships,” said Jhandu.It was a huge gamble and, initially, it appeared to have backfired. He failed to register a successful lift at the competition in New Delhi. But his determination caught the attention of para powerlifting coach Rajinder Singh Rahelu, who invited him to train at the Sports Authority of India’s National Centre of Excellence in Gandhinagar.It proved to be the breakthrough he desperately needed. Later that year, he won a silver medal at the inaugural Khelo India Para Games in New Delhi.Since then, he has not looked back, winning medals at several national and international competitions, including a bronze medal at the Asia-Oceania Open Para Powerlifting Championships in Bangkok in April this year.He secured the podium with a 191kg lift, which also sealed his qualification for the Commonwealth Games. Besides these accomplishments, he also holds the national record in the 72kg category with a lift of 206kg.Now preparing for the biggest competition of his career, Jhandu credits the people who stood by him during the toughest phase of his journey, including his brother, Kundan.“I met people who supported and motivated me. I always believed that if I worked hard enough, I would achieve something. Financial support wasn’t always there, but I had confidence in myself. I kept telling myself that I would succeed one day,” he said.Making it to the Commonwealth Games in itself is a success for a man who never stopped believing in it. On Friday, Jhandu will hope to add a medal to that remarkable journey.Stay Updated With: CWG Schedule 2026
Article Summary: Jhandu Kumar will compete in the men's heavyweight category of para-powerlifting on Friday. The 29-year-old was affected by polio from the age of five. He has won medals at state and national competitions in both para and able-bodied powerlifting. He holds the national record in the 72kg category.

Article Title: Doping cloud darkens India’s CWG start as judoka fails test, lifting quota shrinks
Article Text:
CWG 2026 (IANS Photo)

NEW DELHI: India suffered a doping jolt as the Glasgow Commonwealth Games began on Thursday with the lawn bowls competitions. First came the news that prominent judoka and medal hope Arun Kumar failed the dope test for a banned anabolic steroid in an out-of-competition testing. Hours later, another setback followed as the Indian contingent was forced to surrender one weightlifting quota of Dilbagh Singh because of multiple anti-doping rule violations (ADRVs) committed during the Glasgow CWG qualification period. The developments shrunk the nation’s overall contingent strength to 123 athletes. Para-swimmer Tejas Nandakumar was earlier dropped after failing to meet the classification criteria.TOI had earlier reported that the country’s lifting squad had already been weakened after four national campers — N Ajith (71kg), Sairaj Pardeshi (88kg), Harcharan Singh (110kg) and Vanshita Verma (77kg) — tested positive for prohibited substances before the Games. Ajith and Pardeshi were considered serious gold medal contenders, making their absence a significant blow to India’s medal hopes.India had initially secured 16 lifting quota places, but repeated doping violations during the qualification window from June 1, 2025, to July 22, 2026, triggered an automatic reduction under CWG qualification rules.The country’s allocation first fell to 12 and has now effectively reduced to 11 after Dilbagh was withdrawn from the squad.Under the Glasgow CWG qualification regulations, “every anti-doping rule violation (ADRV) committed by a weightlifter or athlete support personnel between June 1, 2025 and July 22, 2026, and conclusively sanctioned during the same period, results in the country’s weightlifting quota being reduced by one”. Multiple ADRVs attract an equivalent reduction in quota places, a provision that ultimately costs India one slot.Importantly, Dilbagh was not involved in any doping offence. His withdrawal was an administrative consequence of India’s reduced quota. With the lifter struggling with a back injury and unable to train adequately during the preparatory camp in Birmingham, the Indian Weightlifting Federation (IWLF) decided it was prudent to send him home, allowing the remaining medal hopefuls to compete. The decision was conveyed to the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and the chief-de-mission’s (CDM) office in Glasgow.Judoka Arun’s exit is equally damaging. The 21-year-old, who competes in the 73kg category and won gold at last year’s Taipei Asian Open, received a provisional suspension from the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) after returning an adverse analytical finding. The judo squad, which trained at Japan’s Tsukuba University until July 17, is scheduled to leave for Glasgow on July 27 as the competitions begin on July 31.TOI had reported that every CWG-bound athlete underwent two rounds of dope testing before departure, while competitors training overseas were tested through coordination between NADA and anti-doping agencies in their respective host countries.
Article Summary: India suffered a doping jolt as the Glasgow Commonwealth Games began on Thursday with the lawn bowls competitions. First came the news that prominent judoka and medal hope Arun Kumar failed the dope test for a banned anabolic steroid in an out-of-competition testing. Hours later, the Indian contingent was forced to surrender one weightlifting quota of Dilbagh Singh because of multiple anti- doping rule violations.
