Article Title: CWG 2026: Minor para cyclist in ‘emotional distress’ over support staff uncertainty
Article Text:
Lisha Das (Pic credit: NVS India)

NEW DELHI: Claiming that she has been subjected to “mental harassment”, “immense stress” and repeated administrative uncertainty in the final days before the Commonwealth Games, 16-year-old para cyclist Lisha Das has written a fresh, strongly worded email to sports authorities after alleging that her accredited coach, Aditya Mehta, has again been removed from the official list and replaced by a Cycling Federation of India (CFI) executive committee member.The latest dispute centres on the accreditation of support staff. According to Lisha, Mehta — whose inclusion as her coach had earlier been reflected in the squad following proceedings before the Delhi High Court — has now been struck off the accreditation list. In his place, K Dattatraya, a CFI office-bearer, has been listed as both coach and technician. Lisha has objected to the move, maintaining that Dattatraya may accompany the contingent as a technician but cannot replace her coach.The development assumes significance because, under the govt’s policy, National Sports Federation (NSF) office-bearers travel at “no cost to govt”, with their expenses borne by the respective federation. It was for this reason that Dattatraya, a CFI official, had earlier been replaced by Mehta in the contingent, enabling Lisha’s coach to travel in the officially sanctioned coaching role. The latest change has now triggered another confrontation days before the minor para cyclist from Assam leaves for Glasgow.The controversy comes after TOI exclusively highlighted Lisha’s concerns over the absence of a woman support staff member for the minor athlete, following which authorities approved the inclusion of physiotherapist Dr Asha Shaikh. The Delhi HC subsequently granted interim relief, directing authorities to include Mehta as coach, Shaikh as physiotherapist and female support staff, and Dattatraya as technician.In her latest email, accessed by TOI, Lisha wrote, “I’m writing this email with a deeply heavy heart and immense emotional distress. I’m the youngest athlete in this situation and the manner in which this entire matter has been handled has been extremely demotivating and emotionally distressing for me. Yesterday, I was again contacted by officials through a video call on my coach’s phone. I clearly stated that I am a minor and that my coach and Dr Shaikh are the guardians and support persons who have been directly involved in my training, care, and preparation. I requested that any matter concerning me should be discussed directly with them. I respectfully ask: Is this the appropriate way to communicate with and handle a minor athlete?” she further said.Highlighting the impact on her preparation, she added: “I have been trying to focus on my training and competition. However, repeated uncertainty, calls, messages, and administrative hurdles have caused immense stress at a time when I should be preparing to compete and win medals for my country.”Reiterating that the issue had already figured before the Delhi HC, Lisha wrote: “Aditya Mehta is my coach, and this is not a new or recently made claim. His position as my coach is already recorded in the proceedings and documents before the hon’ble HC.”She also questioned why “a different person is suddenly being referred to as my coach”, adding: “If K Dattatraya is being sent as a technician, I have no objection to his role as a technician. A technician and a coach have different roles and responsibilities, and they cannot simply be treated as interchangeable.”The email also contains a sharp message to the authorities. “To my knowledge, I have not received meaningful support from the Govt of India, SAI, PCI, or CFI. Therefore, I respectfully request that the organisations concerned do not claim credit for my achievements,” she wrote, while requesting that her photographs not be used for publicity without her consent.Seeking a final written clarification, Lisha asked whether Mehta would officially be permitted to accompany her. “If the answer is no, I will then make my own travel arrangements,” she wrote, adding that no travel arrangements should be made for Dattatraya, Ramesh Pandi — another technician whose name had been suggested — or Dr Shaikh if her coach was not allowed to travel.“I am an athlete. I need to train, recover, and compete. I should not have to spend the final days before an important international competition dealing with repeated administrative uncertainty and mental harassment. If I am unable to perform at my best, the immense mental pressure and uncertainty I have been subjected to during this period will be a significant reason,” she wrote.The fresh confrontation comes even as the CFI recently wrote to Lisha seeking confirmation of her travel sector to facilitate ticket bookings, while noting that Dr Shaikh’s travel had to be aligned with hers in view of visa requirements. However, Lisha’s latest email indicates that the dispute over her support team remains unresolved.
Article Summary: 16-year-old para cyclist Lisha Das has written a fresh, strongly worded email to sports authorities. She alleges that her accredited coach, Aditya Mehta, has been removed from the official list and replaced by a Cycling Federation of India (CFI) executive committee member. The latest dispute centres on the accreditation of support staff.

Article Title: From Puri to Glasgow, two gymnasts chase CWG dream
Article Text:
(From left) Tapan Mohanty, Rakesh Patra and Tapeshwarnath Das in Glasgow

The squad: Men's Team: Tapan Mohanty, Tapeshwaranath Das, Swathish KP, Yogeshwar Singh

Tapan Mohanty, Tapeshwaranath Das, Swathish KP, Yogeshwar Singh Women's Team: Protistha Samanta, Pranati Nayak, Nishka Agarwal, Eshitaa Rewale

As the Indian gymnasts begin their Commonwealth Games campaign in Glasgow on Friday, two young athletes from Puri, Odisha, will be looking to make their mark on one of the biggest stages of their careers.Tapan Mohanty and Tapeshwarnath Das both took up gymnastics at a young age after joining the State Sports Hostel in the coastal town. Pursuing a sport that still lacks widespread popularity in India was never easy, but they kept their heads down, trusted the process and are now among the four Indian men's gymnasts set to compete at the Commonwealth Games.For Mohanty, making the Commonwealth Games squad is the culmination of years of hard work, and the youngster is quietly confident after an encouraging performance at last month's Asian Championships.“It was a great experience and I performed well there. I competed against Olympians and international medallists, and I learned a lot by watching how they prepared and competed,” said Mohanty.The gymnast, whose father was a servitor at Jagannath Temple and a former state-level wrestler, believes competing against the world's best has also changed his outlook.“Seeing them win medals made me realise that I can do it too. It gave me confidence and reinforced the importance of staying focused and working hard,” he added.An all-round gymnast, Mohanty believes his best chance lies in the floor exercise, where he hopes to qualify for the final and challenge for a medal. He had also represented India at the 2023 Asian Games.Preparing for an event of this magnitude has meant weeks of meticulous planning. After the Asian Championships, the Indian team travelled to Essex in England for a training camp at South Essex Gymnastics Club under coaches Scott Hann and Anthony Wise.For Das, the stint in Essex has been invaluable and he believes it will make a significant difference once competition gets underway in Glasgow.“The facilities are excellent, and we’re training with the same equipment that we'll use during the competition,” Das had said while training there.“We’ve also had enough time to adapt to the weather and conditions here. Had we travelled directly from India, the adjustment would have been much harder. Spending a longer period here has really helped our preparation.”A vault specialist, Das believes the overseas training has further sharpened his strongest event which he loves for the strength and explosiveness associated with it.“Success in vault depends on technique and the execution of skill, and I’ve developed that through years of consistent training,” he said.Apart from hours of practice in the gym, both athletes have also incorporated meditation into their daily routine to stay mentally composed. Equally important has been the bond they share, having grown up in the same city and trained together for nearly a decade.Years after beginning their journeys at State Sports Hostel in Puri, Das and Mohanty now stand on the brink of the biggest competition of their careers. Along with Rakesh Patra, their senior and now coach, they will hope the road from Odisha to Glasgow ends with a performance to remember.
Article Summary: Tapan Mohanty and Tapeshwarnath Das both took up gymnastics at a young age after joining the State Sports Hostel in Puri, Odisha. Pursuing a sport that still lacks widespread popularity in India was never easy, but they kept their heads down. They are now among the four Indian men's gymnasts set to compete at the Commonwealth Games.

Article Title: 'Don't claim credit for my achievements': Para-cyclist questions sports authorities over support staff uncertainty as Commonwealth Games begin
Article Text:
Lisha Das

India's only para-cyclist at the Commonwealth Games, 16-year-old Lisha Das, has written to the country's top sports authorities, saying the uncertainty over her support staff and travel arrangements for Glasgow has caused her "immense emotional distress" just before the start of the Games.Lisha has sent the email to officials of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA), Cycling Federation of India (CFI), Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) and the Sports Ministry.The Commonwealth Games opening ceremony will be held on Thursday night.In her letter, Lisha said she is still waiting for clarity on the approval of her support team, which includes personal coach Aditya Mehta, female physiotherapist Dr Asha Shaikh and an experienced para-cycling technician.While Shaikh's travel was eventually cleared after repeated requests and court intervention, there is still no confirmation over Mehta's travel or accreditation. Instead, authorities have proposed K Dattatraya as technician/coach, even though Lisha had earlier rejected his inclusion in her support team.Lisha said she had specifically requested that Mehta travel with her as coach. Although that request was initially accepted, she has not received any update on his travel arrangements."I am writing this e-mail with a deeply heavy heart and immense emotional distress. As an athlete, my only responsibility should be to concentrate on my training and prepare to represent my country to the best of my ability. However, since May 15, I have been continuously trying to reach the concerned officials and seeking clarity and support regarding my participation and travel arrangements for the Commonwealth Games," Lisha wrote, as quoted by news agency PTI."I have not been seeking financial support for the years of training, equipment, preparation and qualification that have enabled me to reach this level. My coach (Mehta) and his organisation have independently supported me extensively, including my training, equipment and preparation. Despite repeated communications and reminders, instead of receiving clarity, I have faced continued uncertainty and immense mental pressure," she added.Mehta has now decided to arrange the entire support team himself."Lisha is India's youngest and first para cyclist to qualify for the Commonwealth Games, and she is also the first Indian female para cyclist to achieve this qualification. Yet, instead of being allowed to focus on representing the country, this young athlete is now being forced to fight administrative battles on her own," Mehta told PTI."But she will not give up. Lisha will move forward with determination," he added.Lisha said the uncertainty has affected her preparations and left her "extremely demotivated"."Yesterday, I was again contacted by officials through a video call on my coach's phone. I clearly stated that I am a minor and that my coach and Dr Shaikh are the guardians and support persons who have been directly involved in my training, care and preparation."I requested that any matter concerning me should be discussed directly with them."I have been trying to focus on my training and competition. However, repeated uncertainty, calls, messages and administrative hurdles have caused immense stress at a time when I should be preparing to compete and win medals for my country," she wrote.Lisha also pointed out that Mehta's role as her coach had already been recorded during proceedings before the Delhi High Court."Despite the court proceedings and the orders passed by the Hon'ble High Court, I have continued to face immense uncertainty, repeated communications and what I feel has been considerable mental harassment regarding the very same issue of my coach and support team."I fail to understand why, despite the matter being before the Hon'ble High Court and the position of my coach being recorded on the court record, I am still being subjected to this level of uncertainty and pressure immediately before an important international competition," she said.She clarified that she had no objection to Dattatraya travelling as a technician but insisted that his role could not replace that of her coach."If K. Dattatraya is being sent as a technician, I have no objection to his role as a technician. However, I need my coach, Aditya Mehta, to accompany me as my coach, along with any required technician or other support personnel."A technician and a coach have different roles and responsibilities, and they cannot simply be treated as interchangeable," she wrote.Lisha further said that if Mehta is not allowed to accompany her, she will arrange her own travel.She cautioned that she would "not be travelling under the banner or financial support of the Government of India, SAI, PCI or CFI"."I will make my own travel arrangements and travel at my own expense," she said.Lisha also claimed that she had "not received meaningful support from the Government of India, SAI, PCI or CFI for the competitions, equipment and preparation through which I have reached this level"."I respectfully request that the organisations concerned do not claim credit for my achievements. I also request that my photographs and personal images not be used for publicity or promotional purposes without my consent."
Article Summary: 16-year-old Lisha Das is India's only para-cyclist at the Commonwealth Games. She has written to the country's top sports authorities, saying uncertainty over her support staff has caused her "immense emotional distress" Lisha said she is still waiting for clarity on the approval of her support team, which includes personal coach Aditya Mehta.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Dilbag Singh withdraws as India's weightlifting quota reduced over doping violations
Article Text:
Dilbag Singh withdraws from Commonwealth Games 2026 (Image: X)

Dilbag Singh Withdrawn



Mirabai Chanu to Lead India's Campaign



India's weightlifting contingent for the 2026 Commonwealth Games has suffered a major setback after the country's athlete quota was reduced because of multiple anti-doping rule violations (ADRVs) during the qualification period. As a result, Dilbag Singh has been withdrawn from the squad, leaving India with an 11-member team for the Glasgow Games.The Indian Weightlifting Federation (IWLF) had initially announced a 12-member squad led by Tokyo Olympic silver medallist Mirabai Chanu . However, the federation was informed only on Wednesday that India's quota had been reduced by one athlete due to its doping record during the qualification cycle.With the quota reduced, the federation decided to withdraw Dilbag Singh, who has been struggling with a back injury. According to officials, the lifter was unable to train during the national preparatory camp in Birmingham, making him the logical choice to miss out on the Games.India's reduced quota stems from multiple anti-doping offences committed by weightlifters during the qualification period. Among those sanctioned were N. Ajith (71kg), Sairaj Pardeshi (88kg) and Harcharan Singh (110kg), who were handed bans ahead of the Commonwealth Games.Vanshita Verma (86kg) also faced sanctions for violating anti-doping regulations.The repeated violations prompted Commonwealth authorities to reduce India's weightlifting allocation, dealing another blow to a sport that has repeatedly faced scrutiny over doping issues in recent years.Despite the reduction in quota, India will still field a strong weightlifting contingent led by Mirabai Chanu, one of the country's brightest medal hopes at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games.
Article Summary: Dilbag Singh withdraws from India's weightlifting squad for 2026 Commonwealth Games. India's athlete quota was reduced because of multiple anti-doping rule violations (ADRVs) during the qualification period. Dilbag Singh has been withdrawn from the squad, leaving India with an 11-member team for the Glasgow Games.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Putul Sonowal stuns world champion Ryan Bester in lawn bowls thriller
Article Text:
Putul Sonowal (X Photo)

Rupa Rani-Pinki survive thriller in Women's Pairs



NEW DELHI: India made a sensational start to their Glasgow Commonwealth Games 2026 campaign as lawn bowler Putul Sonowal pulled off a stunning upset against reigning world champion Ryan Bester of Canada in the Men's Singles competition on Thursday.Making his Commonwealth Games debut, the Assam-born bowler showed remarkable composure to defeat one of the biggest names in the sport, winning the contest in a tense tie-break after both players shared the opening two sets.Sonowal, the reigning Asian champion, won the first set 5-4 before Bester responded strongly with a dominant 7-3 victory in the second set to force a decider.However, the Indian kept his calm when it mattered most, edging the tie-break to complete a memorable victory in his opening match of Section D.The win was particularly significant given Bester's decorated career. The Canadian has won multiple Commonwealth Games medals, including a bronze in Men's Singles in 2006 and silver medals in 2014 and 2018. He also boasts seven World Outdoor Championships medals, including a Singles gold in 2023, and was inducted into the inaugural World Bowls Hall of Fame class in 2025.Sonowal will next face Cecil Alexander of Falkland Islands on Friday.India's strong start continued in the Women's Pairs event, where the experienced duo of Rupa Rani Tirkey and Pinki Singh defeated Malta in another dramatic tie-break encounter.The Indian pair began brilliantly at the Scottish Event Campus (SEC) Hall 3, winning the opening set 7-1 against Malta's Rebecca Louise Rixon and Connie-Leigh Rixon.But Malta fought back in the second set, winning 4-3 to take the match into a deciding tie-break. In a tense finish, India found themselves trailing before Pinki delivered a brilliant final bowl to seal victory.In lawn bowls, the skip is the team captain who decides strategy and plays the final two bowls of an end, while the lead delivers the first bowl and focuses on positioning near the target.The Indian Women's Pairs team will now face South Africa in their second Section B match on Friday.Both Tirkey and Pinki were members of India's historic gold medal-winning Women's Fours team at the 2022 Birmingham Commonwealth Games. However, the Fours events have been removed from the Glasgow edition, leaving only Men's and Women's Singles and Pairs competitions.India had also won a silver medal in the Men's Fours event at Birmingham, and Sonowal's stunning opening victory has raised hopes of another strong lawn bowls campaign.
Article Summary: Putul Sonowal beats world champion Ryan Bester of Canada in Men's Singles. Assam-born bowler wins contest in a tense tie-break after both players shared the opening two sets. Indian duo of Rupa Rani Tirkey and Pinki Singh defeat Malta in Women's Pairs.

Article Title: Indian judoka Arun Kumar withdrawn from 2026 Commonwealth Games after failing dope test
Article Text:
Arun Kumar

India's Commonwealth Games contingent has suffered a setback on the day of the Glasgow 2026 opening ceremony, with judoka Arun Kumar withdrawn from the competition after failing a dope test.The rising 73kg judoka was declared ineligible following an adverse analytical finding in an out-of-competition test conducted by the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA).His withdrawal reduces India's athlete contingent from 125 to 124.Arun had been one of India's brightest medal prospects in judo after enjoying a rapid rise through the junior and senior ranks.Training at the Inspire Institute of Sport, he won gold at the 2023 Macau Junior Asian Cup, followed by another gold at the 2025 Taipei Asian Open and a bronze at the Hong Kong Asian Open.Earlier this year, he also finished seventh at the prestigious Tashkent Grand Slam, earning his maiden Commonwealth Games selection.Arun's withdrawal comes despite strict anti-doping checks carried out before the Games. Indian athletes underwent two rounds of testing before leaving for Glasgow, while those training overseas were tested in coordination with anti-doping agencies in their host countries.The increased vigilance followed several recent doping cases, particularly in weightlifting, where multiple Indian lifters tested positive before the Games, reducing the country's weightlifting quota from 16 to 12 athletes.Along with NADA, the Athletics Integrity Unit and national sports federations monitored athletes and educated them about anti-doping rules before the Games.India had originally cleared a 126-member athlete contingent for Glasgow. Following recent withdrawals, including Arun Kumar's, the country's squad has now been reduced to 124 competitors.
Article Summary: Arun Kumar has withdrawn from the Commonwealth Games after failing a dope test. The rising 73kg judoka was declared ineligible following an adverse analytical finding in an out-of-competition test conducted by the National Anti-Doping Agency. His withdrawal reduces India's athlete contingent from 125 to 124.

Article Title: India's first CWG 2026 medal is already assured before the opening ceremony - Here's how
Article Text:
Lovlina Borgohain (PTI Photo)

NEW DELHI: India has secured its first medal at the Commonwealth Games 2026 even before the opening ceremony, with Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain guaranteed at least a bronze in the women's boxing competition.The Assam boxer received a direct entry into the semifinals after being handed a bye in her 75kg weight category. As all losing semifinalists receive bronze medals in Commonwealth Games boxing, Lovlina is now assured of a place on the podium before stepping into the ring.She will begin her campaign on July 31, when she takes on T.K.B.P. Taafaki for a place in the gold medal bout.Lovlina's assured medal gives India an early boost ahead of the official start of the Games, where the country has sent a 124-member contingent to Glasgow.Although the 2026 edition features a reduced sports programme, India will still compete across several disciplines with hopes of adding to its rich Commonwealth Games legacy.India's campaign begins on Thursday with two lawn bowls matches before the opening ceremony later in the day.The contingent will compete in eight sports for able-bodied athletes—athletics, boxing, weightlifting, judo, artistic gymnastics, track cycling, bowls and swimming—alongside five para disciplines, including para-athletics, para-powerlifting, para-swimming, para-track cycling and 3x3 wheelchair basketball.Athletics action will run from July 27 to August 1, with Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra among the biggest attractions. The reigning world champion will look to reclaim the Commonwealth title he won at Gold Coast 2018 after missing Birmingham 2022 through injury.Weightlifting is expected to be another key source of medals for India, with Olympic silver medallist and two-time Commonwealth Games champion Mirabai Chanu leading the challenge.With Lovlina already assured of a podium finish, India has made a dream start to its Glasgow 2026 campaign even before the Games have officially begun.
Article Summary: Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain guaranteed at least a bronze in the women's boxing competition. Assam boxer received a direct entry into the semifinals after being handed a bye in her 75kg weight category. India's campaign begins on Thursday with two lawn bowls matches before the opening ceremony.

Article Title: CWG 2026: India's wheelchair basketball team ready to script history on debut
Article Text:
Representational photo

Four women. Four different battles. One shared dream, to script history in Glasgow. India will make their CWG debut in women’s 3x3 wheelchair basketball against Wales on July 25, a day after the competition begins. For captain Minakshi Harichandra Jadhav, Irengbam Ritu Chanu, Reena Rameshchandra Gupta and Laxmi Rayappa Rayannavar, the occasion will be the culmination of years of grit, rehabilitation and relentless perseverance.India qualified through the IWBF 3x3 Asia-Oceania zonal qualifier in Bangkok alongside Australia. The two were the only entrants in the women’s competition and secured the qualification places for Asia and Oceania respectively.For Minakshi, who hails from Maharashtra’s Satara district, life changed forever in 2012. “I was a normal village girl. After falling from a tree, I suffered a spinal cord injury and gradually lost sensation below my waist. There was a time when I was in the ICU, but rehabilitation changed my life,” she said.At a rehabilitation centre in Mumbai, she met former players, coaches and social workers who encouraged her to take up the sport.“The rehabilitation centre, my coaches and the Wheelchair Basketball Federation of India stood by me. We have one goal now - to win a medal in Glasgow and make India proud,” the captain said.Ritu’s journey has been equally remarkable. The Manipur athlete lost her right leg above the knee after being hit by a reversing bus when she was barely seven. Having represented India at the Asia-Oceania qualifier, she now balances training with weaving at home to support herself. “My sister, the state govt and my weaving work keep me going. Representing India makes every struggle worthwhile,” she said.Karnataka’s Laxmi, who was affected by polio at birth, overcame a difficult childhood before discovering wheelchair basketball in 2019. A postgraduate, she said: “People who once doubted me now see what is possible. This is my first international tournament and I want to make it count.”
Article Summary: India will make their CWG debut in women’s 3x3 wheelchair basketball against Wales on July 25, a day after the competition begins. Captain Minakshi Harichandra Jadhav, Irengbam Ritu Chanu, Reena Rameshchandra Gupta and Laxmi Rayappa Rayannavar will all play.

Article Title: 'Replay the final': More than 88,000 Argentina fans call for replay after bitter World Cup final defeat
Article Text:
Argentina's Lionel Messi (10) cries at the end of the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough)

Petition accuses referee of "controversial and corrupt" performance

88,000 Argentina fans demand World Cup final replay after 'controversial and corrupt' referee claims

Spain dominated before sealing victory in extra time

Fans watch the World Cup final soccer match between Argentina and Spain in Buenos Aires, Argentina, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Gustavo Garello)

Tempers boiled over after the final whistle

Similar replay campaign emerged earlier in the tournament

Spain's dramatic 1-0 extra-time victory over Argentina in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final may have settled the destination of the trophy, but the controversy surrounding the showpiece continues to gather momentum days after the final whistle.A petition demanding that the World Cup final be replayed has now attracted 88,915 signatures at the time of writing, with thousands of Argentina supporters claiming the match was influenced by controversial refereeing decisions.The online campaign, launched on Change.org by Argentine supporter Gisela Sánchez, calls on FIFA to review the officiating performance of Slovenian referee Slavko Vinčić, who oversaw Sunday's final at the New York New Jersey Stadium.Spain secured their second men's World Cup title courtesy of Ferran Torres' 106th-minute winner after extra time, ending Argentina's hopes of defending the trophy they won four years earlier.However, the result has not been accepted by a section of Argentina supporters.In the petition , Sánchez alleges that Vinčić delivered a "controversial and corrupt" performance and urges FIFA to investigate several key decisions made during the final."The recent final between Argentina and Spain was tarnished by the controversial and corrupt performance of the referee who, according to video evidence, was bought to influence the match's outcome," the petition states."It is a monumental disappointment for the players, coaches, and, above all, for the fans who crave to see a game decided by talent and dedication on the pitch, and not by rigged refereeing decisions."If we allow corruption to go unnoticed on this global stage, we are setting a bad example for future generations of athletes and fans."Therefore, we ask FIFA to review these incidents with seriousness and transparency, and to consider replaying the final, this time without the influence of a corrupt referee."The petition, however, does not provide independently verified evidence to support those allegations beyond videos circulating across social media which the organiser claims favour Spain.Despite the reaction from some supporters, Spain were widely viewed as the better side throughout the final.Luis de la Fuente's team controlled possession for long spells, pinned Argentina deep inside their own half and prevented the defending champions from registering a single shot on target during normal time.Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez repeatedly kept Argentina in the contest before Ferran Torres finally broke the deadlock in the 106th minute of extra time.Argentina's task had already become significantly harder after midfielder Enzo Fernández was sent off in the third minute of stoppage time at the end of normal time.Having already been booked for dissent following a denied free-kick, Fernández received a second yellow card after a reckless challenge on Spain defender Pau Cubarsí, reducing Lionel Scaloni's side to ten men before extra time began.According to match statistics, Vinčić awarded 46 fouls during the final, with 25 committed by Argentina as the match became increasingly fragmented.The frustration carried over into the closing moments of the evening.Immediately after Spain were confirmed as world champions, ugly scenes erupted on the pitch.Leandro Paredes was sent off after the final whistle following clashes involving Eric García and Gavi, while Nahuel Molina also appeared to spark part of the confrontation after confronting Spain captain Rodri.The incidents have since become the subject of a separate FIFA disciplinary review.Speaking during ITV's coverage, former England defender Gary Neville strongly criticised Argentina's conduct."It's a disgrace," Neville said."I love the competitiveness of the Argentines, fighting and scrapping for their lives every game. Messi's propped them up at times and they're very competitive and I love that element of them."But it's been a disgrace the last few games."The Argentina petition is not the first online campaign calling for a World Cup replay during this tournament.Following Spain's semi-final victory over France, French supporters launched a similar Change.org petition after disputing a controversial incident that led to the penalty opening the scoring.That campaign also gathered more than 82,000 signatures, although it had no effect on FIFA's official result.Likewise, there is no indication that the latest petition will alter the outcome of the World Cup final.Meanwhile, Change.org has also hosted petitions taking the opposite position. One campaign calling for Argentina to be banned from future World Cups amassed more than 29 million signatures before eventually being closed.Away from the online debate, thousands of Argentina supporters gathered across the country following the team's return home, applauding Lionel Scaloni's squad for reaching a second consecutive World Cup final despite falling just short of retaining their title against an impressive Spanish side.
Article Summary: 88,000 Argentina fans demand World Cup final replay after 'controversial and corrupt' referee claims. Spain secured their second men's World Cup title courtesy of Ferran Torres' 106th-minute winner after extra time. However, the result has not been accepted by a section of Argentina supporters.

Article Title: Italy sound out Pep Guardiola, Ancelotti in search for new national team coach
Article Text:
Pep Guardiola

The Italian Football Federation (FIGC) has held talks with former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola and Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti as it looks for a new national team coach following Italy's failure to qualify for the FIFA World Cup for a third straight time.The federation hopes to appoint a new coach within the week as it looks to rebuild after another disappointing qualifying campaign.Former Italy and AC Milan defender Paolo Maldini, who was appointed the federation's technical director earlier this month, attended a meeting with Serie A clubs on Thursday alongside new FIGC president Giovanni Malagò and special advisor Leonardo.Asked about Guardiola after the meeting, Maldini confirmed that the Spaniard is among the candidates but said the process is still ongoing."Honestly, today we can't give news about what's happening. You've identified one of our targets," Maldini said."We can't hide that we also talked with Carlo Ancelotti before talking with Pep. Honestly, it seemed right to start with the best in the world, to see their general availability."Guardiola left Manchester City at the end of last season after spending 10 years at the club, winning 35 major trophies across his managerial career with Barcelona, Bayern Munich and City.According to Maldini, he and Leonardo spent three days in Barcelona meeting Guardiola to discuss the Italy job."The best thing would be to announce the new coach this week, but even more to wait for the person we really want," Maldini said. "So there's urgency, but not so much inside us."Ancelotti, meanwhile, signed a contract extension with Brazil in May that runs until the 2030 World Cup. However, Brazil endured one of its poorest World Cup campaigns this year, exiting in the round of 16 after a 2-1 defeat to Norway.The 67-year-old has won league titles in Italy, England, France, Spain and Germany, and remains the only coach to have won the UEFA Champions League five times.Italy's failure to qualify for the World Cup after losing the playoff to Bosnia and Herzegovina in March led to the resignations of FIGC president Gabriele Gravina and head coach Gennaro Gattuso.
Article Summary: Italian Football Federation holds talks with Pep Guardiola and Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti. Italy failed to qualify for the FIFA World Cup for a third straight time. The federation hopes to appoint a new coach within the week. Former Italy and AC Milan defender Paolo Maldini attended a meeting with Serie A clubs on Thursday.

Article Title: Spain's World Cup triumph ends with players receiving their body weight in tomatoes
Article Text:
Spain stars Fabián Ruiz and Gavi receive bodyweight in tomatoes after World Cup triumph as hometown honours champions/ Image: lospalacios

A hometown celebration unlike any other

A tradition dating back to Spain's golden generation









Spain's triumph also brings a major financial reward

Spain's Rodri (16) lifts the trophy as Spain celebrates after winning the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Ashley Landis)

Spain's World Cup triumph has brought medals, global recognition and record prize money, but for Fabián Ruiz and Gavi, one of the most memorable rewards arrived hundreds of miles from New York New Jersey Stadium.Just days after helping Spain defeat Argentina 1-0 after extra time to win the 2026 FIFA World Cup, the two midfielders returned to their hometown of Los Palacios y Villafranca, where they were welcomed with one of Spanish football's most unusual traditions — receiving their own body weight in tomatoes.The pair were honoured during an official civic reception after returning to Los Palacios y Villafranca, a town of fewer than 40,000 residents located south of Seville, which has become synonymous with producing elite Spanish footballers.Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Fabián Ruiz and Barcelona star Gavi arrived wearing their World Cup winners' medals after playing key roles in Spain's successful campaign in North America.Ruiz started the World Cup final against Argentina, while Gavi featured throughout another impressive international tournament as Luis de la Fuente's side captured Spain's second men's World Cup title thanks to Ferran Torres' 106th-minute winner in New Jersey.As part of the ceremony, the traditional weigh-in of the athletes took place, where they were presented with their weight in the most emblematic product of local agriculture. The Los Palacios Tomato Producers Association, joined the Town Hall in organising the tribute.Ruiz tipped the scales at 85 kilograms, while Gavi weighed 68.5 kilograms, with both players receiving those exact amounts in BombónColorao tomatoes. The gesture has become a hallmark of the municipality in recognising its most distinguished athletes.The ceremony also featured former Spain winger Jesús Navas, who became the first footballer from Los Palacios y Villafranca to win the FIFA World Cup when Spain lifted the trophy in South Africa in 2010.Navas had previously received the same tomato tribute after helping Spain win Euro 2024, alongside Ruiz.The town has continued expanding its tributes to its footballing heroes.The local sports pavilion already carries the names of Jesús Navas and Fabián Ruiz, while officials confirmed that football fields will now also be renamed in honour of Gavi following Spain's latest World Cup success.In a statement , the town council also revealed longer-term plans to commemorate all three champions."In addition, the town hall will promote the construction of a monument dedicated to the three champions from Los Palacios."The statement added: "In this way, the city council wants to pay permanent tribute to three athletes who represent the pride of an entire town and who, with their sporting and human trajectory, have become role models for several generations of children and young people."The celebrations come after Spain secured one of the most lucrative prizes in international football.Ferran Torres' extra-time strike against Argentina not only delivered Spain's second World Cup title but also earned the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) FIFA's winners' prize of $51 million. According to AS, Spain's players will each receive a substantial share of that prize under a bonus agreement negotiated between the squad captains and the RFEF before the tournament.Unlike paying federations after every knockout round, FIFA awards a single payment based on a team's final finishing position.Simply reaching the World Cup final had already guaranteed Spain $34 million. Under the agreement, 40 per cent of that amount would have been distributed among the players, creating a bonus pool worth approximately $13.6 million, or just over $523,000 per player before taxes across the 26-man squad.Winning the final increased those figures even further.Under the same agreement, the players became entitled to 45 per cent of FIFA's winners' prize, creating a dressing-room bonus pool worth approximately $22.95 million.That means each member of Spain's 26-player squad is expected to receive around $882,700 (€760,000) before taxes, according to AS.The remaining prize money will stay with the RFEF, helping cover the federation's World Cup expenses while also being reinvested into the development of Spanish football, including strengthening the federation's infrastructure and supporting grassroots programmes across the country.For Ruiz and Gavi, however, the homecoming demonstrated that not every reward is measured in prize money. Alongside their World Cup medals and sizeable bonuses, they returned to the town where their football journeys began to receive a distinctly local honour, one measured in kilograms of tomatoes rather than trophies.
Article Summary: Spain stars Fabián Ruiz and Gavi receive bodyweight in tomatoes after World Cup triumph as hometown honours champions. The two midfielders returned to their hometown of Los Palacios y Villafranca, where they were welcomed with one of Spanish football's most unusual traditions. The gesture has become a hallmark of the municipality in recognising its most distinguished athletes.

Article Title: 'The whole game at risk': Norway prepares ethics complaint over FIFA president's handling of Donald Trump intervention
Article Text:
FILE - President Donald Trump holds up a red card during a meeting with FIFA president Gianni Infantino in the Oval Office of the White House, Tuesday, Aug. 28, 2018, in Washington. (AP Photo/Evan Vucci, File)

How the Balogun controversy unfolded

United States' Folarin Balogun (20) reacts after scoring his team's first goal during the World Cup round of 32 soccer match between the United States and Bosnia in Santa Clara, Calif., near San Francisco, Wednesday, July 1, 2026. (AP Photo/Julio Cortez)

Norway weighs formal ethics action

President Donald Trump is presented with the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize by FIFA President Gianni Infantino during the 2026 FIFA World Cup draw at the Kennedy Center, Friday, Dec. 5, 2025, in Washington. (AP Photo/Evan Vucci)

Klaveness calls for FIFA to admit its mistake

Trump and FIFA defend the decision

Backlash from across European football

The controversy surrounding Folarin Balogun's suspended World Cup ban continues to escalate even after the conclusion of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, with the Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) confirming it is considering filing a formal ethics complaint against FIFA over the handling of the case.According to the BBC, the NFF will decide at its next board meeting whether to submit an official complaint to FIFA's Ethics Committee after raising what it described as "strong concern" over the decision to suspend Balogun's automatic one-match ban following intervention from United States President Donald Trump The case has become one of the most contentious off-field stories of the tournament and has intensified scrutiny of FIFA president Gianni Infantino, whose leadership has already attracted criticism over several decisions made during the World Cup.United States striker Folarin Balogun was shown a straight red card during his side's 2-0 victory over Bosnia and Herzegovina in the Round of 32.Under FIFA regulations, the dismissal carried an automatic one-match suspension, which meant Balogun was expected to miss the United States' Round of 16 clash against Belgium.Instead, FIFA suspended the ban for 12 months, allowing Balogun to remain eligible.No detailed explanation accompanied the decision beyond citing a disciplinary rule that allows punishments to be suspended under certain circumstances.The ruling came after President Trump publicly acknowledged contacting Infantino to request a review of the incident.Balogun ultimately started the knockout tie, although Belgium comfortably defeated the United States 4-1.In a statement provided to the BBC , Norwegian Football Federation president Lise Klaveness confirmed the governing body is seriously considering escalating the matter."The federation reacted with strong concern," Klaveness said, adding that a final decision on submitting an ethics complaint will be made during the federation's next board meeting.The proposed complaint would also be linked to an earlier submission Norway lodged concerning FIFA's decision to award its inaugural Peace Prize to President Trump before the tournament."It is appropriate to include the Balogun case in the inquiry to FIFA's ethics committee that we made before the World Cup regarding FIFA's so-called peace prize award during the draw in Washington before Christmas last year," Klaveness told the BBC.The report also noted that the International Olympic Committee could examine the situation because Infantino has served as an IOC member since 2020.Section Two of the Olympic Charter states that IOC members "will not accept from governments, organisations, or other parties, any mandate or instructions liable to interfere with the freedom of their action and vote."Speaking separately to The Times , Klaveness urged Infantino to publicly acknowledge that FIFA had handled the Balogun case incorrectly."When you bend a rule like this, you're on a slippery slope that will put the whole game at risk," she said."It is a worry for the game when you compromise fundamental rules of the game."She continued: "First of all, it should not have happened. It is very important now to have honest communication around it. We all know that this verdict was influenced from external forces and did not have the proper process.""We need our leader in FIFA to say that this was an error."Klaveness also warned that allowing political influence to shape sporting decisions could have long-term consequences."If you start to adapt in such a way towards state leaders and state politics, you will move your behaviour and the organisation's behaviour, and also the red line of what states' leaders should interfere with. And that happened."She added: "When you make controversial decisions, and when there has been an external, very powerful voice in your ear, it's very important that you have more voices making the decision. And if you don't, it's a mistake.""This case was so serious and so worrying that I hope that it might contribute to bring people out a little bit and don't fear to bring up cases. I will bring it to a board meeting and discuss with my board, and then we do it. To me, it should be in the same sphere of ethical complaint."The controversy stems from comments made by President Trump during an Oval Office press conference on July 6, when he confirmed he had personally spoken with Infantino about Balogun's dismissal."I spoke to Gianni," Trump said."So I saw the play, and I'm a person that loves sports and I understand sports really well, and that wasn't a foul.""Yes, I asked for a review by FIFA. I spoke to a man who is highly respected. I asked for a review because I didn't think it was a foul. I didn't tell him what to do, I can't tell him what to do."Trump later described FIFA's decision to reinstate Balogun as a "great decision."Infantino has consistently maintained that FIFA's judicial bodies operate independently despite the widespread criticism.Norway is not alone in questioning FIFA's handling of the incident.The Royal Belgian Football Federation said it was "deeply concerned by the course of events" and vowed to continue fighting "in defence of the fundamental principles of ethics, fair competition, and the interests of football as a whole."Belgium also requested a formal explanation for the suspended ban, but FIFA ruled the request "inadmissible," leaving the federation without any avenue for appeal.UEFA was equally critical, accusing FIFA of having "crossed a red line" and describing the ruling as an "unprecedented, incomprehensible and unjustifiable decision."The controversy has continued to gather momentum in the days following the World Cup final, with La Liga president Javier Tebas also calling for Infantino to resign over what he described as damage caused to the integrity of the game.With Norway now preparing to discuss formal ethics proceedings, the Balogun case looks set to remain one of the defining controversies of the 2026 World Cup long after Spain lifted the trophy in New Jersey.
Article Summary: Norway considers filing formal ethics complaint against FIFA. Norwegian Football Federation president Lise Klaveness calls for FIFA to admit its mistake. United States striker Folarin Balogun was shown a straight red card during his side's 2-0 victory over Bosnia and Herzegovina in the Round of 32. Under FIFA regulations, the dismissal carried an automatic one-match suspension. Instead, FIFA suspended the ban for 12 months allowing Balogun to remain eligible.

Article Title: 'It will be a tragedy': Cristiano Ronaldo's retirement could cost Portugal millions, marketing expert warns
Article Text:
Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo (AP Photo)

'It will be a tragedy when he leaves'



More than a footballer: Ronaldo's brand will outlive his career



Portugal could face a major commercial and visibility crisis once Cristiano Ronaldo brings down the curtain on his international career, with a leading marketing expert warning that the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) risks losing millions in revenue and global attention if it fails to prepare for life after its greatest-ever player.While Ronaldo has yet to confirm when he will retire from international football, the 41-year-old revealed during the 2026 FIFA World Cup that it would be his final appearance at the tournament. Portugal's last-16 exit against eventual champions Spain has only intensified questions about what comes next for both the legendary forward and the national team.According to Daniel Sá, executive director of the Portuguese Institute of Marketing Administration (IPAM), the FPF faces an enormous branding challenge once Ronaldo eventually steps away."It might be a bit harsh to say, but from a brand perspective, Ronaldo is incomparably bigger than the entire Portuguese national team and countless others combined," Sá told Lusa news agency.Sá believes Ronaldo's influence stretches far beyond goals, trophies and records. The Al Nassr forward, he argues, has become the face of Portuguese football for more than two decades, driving sponsorships, television audiences and commercial partnerships unlike any other player."I'm not making a sporting analysis, but a brand analysis: it will be a tragedy when he leaves, because people still don't grasp the media attention that will be lost. We'll be falling down a high-speed escalator."The marketing expert added that Ronaldo has been the driving force behind the FPF's commercial success."He's the one who makes them sign numerous contracts and earn a lot of money for over 20 years."Sá urged the federation to begin building a fresh identity before Ronaldo's departure becomes official."I believe the FPF is preparing a different narrative, because it can't be dependent on just one person and needs to present other types of arguments. Obviously, there are more to Portuguese football than Ronaldo, but they should explore this new strategy well."According to Sá, Ronaldo's value is no longer defined solely by his performances on the pitch.With more than one billion followers across social media platforms, the five-time Ballon d'Or winner has evolved into one of the most influential sporting figures in history. His global sponsorship portfolio, business ventures and digital reach make him one of football's most powerful commercial assets."Alongside the player, there is Ronaldo the influencer, who is the biggest in the world and the most followed person on social media, Ronaldo sponsored by several national and international brands, and Ronaldo the investor in multiple industries."Sá believes that influence will only continue after retirement: "After he stops playing, this brand will continue to grow."The FPF itself has acknowledged Ronaldo's unmatched commercial value. Chief marketing and commercial officer João Medeiros Cardoso recently admitted the federation would have been "very stupid" not to build campaigns around Ronaldo, particularly during the 2026 World Cup in the United States, one of football's biggest commercial markets.Cardoso also stressed that while younger stars such as Nuno Mendes, Vitinha and Bruno Fernandes will lead Portugal into a new footballing era, replacing Ronaldo's cultural and commercial influence is virtually impossible."We cannot compare that with anybody else," Cardoso said. "When we are talking about Messi and Cristiano, we are talking about the most influential people probably in history."
Article Summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has yet to confirm when he will retire from international football. The 41-year-old revealed during the 2026 FIFA World Cup that it would be his final appearance at the tournament. Marketing expert Daniel Sá warns that Portugal could lose millions in revenue and global attention if it fails to prepare.

Article Title: After 14 years of Didier Deschamps, France set to announce Zinedine Zidane as new head coach
Article Text:
Zinedine Zidane. (Reuters Photo)

Deschamps leaves behind a lasting legacy

Zidane returns to management

Attention turns to nations league fixtures

French football is on the verge of a new chapter, with the French Football Federation (FFF) set to unveil its new men's national team head coach on Tuesday. Former Real Madrid boss and France legend Zinedine Zidane is widely expected to succeed Didier Deschamps, whose 14-year tenure came to an end following the 2026 FIFA World Cup.The announcement will be made by FFF president Philippe Diallo during a press conference at the federation's headquarters in Paris. Although the governing body has not officially confirmed Zidane's appointment, the 54-year-old has emerged as the overwhelming favourite to take charge of Les Bleus.Deschamps stepped down after leading France to another deep World Cup run, with Les Bleus bowing out in the semifinals before finishing fourth in the tournament. During his time in charge, Deschamps restored France's status among international football's elite. He guided the team to the 2018 FIFA World Cup title, the 2022 World Cup final, the UEFA Euro 2016 final, and the 2021 UEFA Nations League crown, making him one of the country's most successful managers.Zidane will return to coaching for the first time since leaving Real Madrid in 2021. His managerial career at the Spanish giants was one of the most successful in modern football, highlighted by three consecutive UEFA Champions League titles between 2016 and 2018.In addition to European success, Zidane also won two La Liga titles, two UEFA Super Cups, two FIFA Club World Cups and multiple domestic honours during his two spells at the Santiago Bernabéu.The France job has long been viewed as the next logical step in Zidane's coaching career, with speculation surrounding his appointment continuing for several years.Before establishing himself as an elite manager, Zidane enjoyed an iconic playing career with the French national team. He inspired France to its maiden FIFA World Cup triumph in 1998, scoring twice in the final against Brazil, before playing a pivotal role in the country's UEFA Euro 2000 success. His performances earned him the 1998 Ballon d'Or, recognising him as the world's best footballer.Zidane represented France in 108 international matches, scoring 31 goals. His final appearance came in the 2006 FIFA World Cup final against Italy, where he was sent off in extra time following the infamous incident involving Marco Materazzi.France's new coach is expected to take charge ahead of the upcoming UEFA Nations League matches. Les Bleus are scheduled to face Turkey away on September 25, followed by another away fixture against Belgium on September 28. They will then host Italy at the Stade de France on October 2.
Article Summary: France legend Zinedine Zidane is expected to take charge of Les Bleus. The 54-year-old will succeed Didier Deschamps, who stepped down after 14 years in charge of the national team. The announcement will be made by FFF president Philippe Diallo at a press conference on Tuesday.

Article Title: 'P*** Espanya': Spain's Ferran Torres World Cup mural vandalised in Barcelona
Article Text:
Ferran Torres World Cup mural vandalised in Barcelona

A mural celebrating Spain's World Cup-winning hero Ferran Torres was vandalised less than 24 hours after it appeared in Barcelona, according to a report from Spanish outlet Dairo AS.The artwork, created by Barcelona-based street artist TVBoy in the city's Gràcia neighbourhood, honoured Torres after he scored the winning goal in Spain's 2026 World Cup final victory over Argentina.The mural showed Torres kissing the World Cup trophy with the words "Making history" and two stars representing Spain's two World Cup titles. It also came after Torres celebrated the title wearing a hat that read "Make Spain Great Again."Soon after it was unveiled, the mural was painted over several times. The first graffiti read "P*** Espanya," before it was replaced with "Espanya".By Wednesday morning, the wall displayed the message "volem seleccions catalanes" ("we want Catalan national teams"), reflecting ongoing political tensions around Catalan identity.Barcelona City Council later stepped in, cleaning the wall and repainting it black.TVBoy said the mural had already made an impact before it was vandalised.Recalling a moment while he was painting, he said, "A girl passed by and shouted; 'Mom, it’s Ferran Torres!' I smiled. Then I understood that art also connects generations."Despite lasting little more than a day, the mural sparked conversation beyond football, highlighting how sport, art and politics often intersect in Barcelona.
Article Summary: Ferran Torres mural vandalised less than 24 hours after it appeared in Barcelona. The artwork was created by Barcelona-based street artist TVBoy. It honoured Torres after he scored the winning goal in Spain's 2026 World Cup final victory over Argentina.

Article Title: 'I'm sorry': Why Argentina's assistant coach Roberto Ayala apologised after FIFA World Cup final
Article Text:
PTI Photo

Chaos after the final whistle



Ayala apologises for his actions



NEW DELHI: Argentina assistant coach Roberto Ayala has apologised for his altercation with Spain midfielder Dani Olmo after the FIFA World Cup 2026 final, admitting that his actions were unacceptable. The ugly scenes unfolded after Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 in extra time on Sunday to lift the World Cup title.FIFA has since launched an investigation into the post-match brawl.Tensions boiled over immediately after the final whistle as players and staff from both teams became involved in heated confrontations.Spain captain Rodri was seen arguing with Argentina defender Nicolas Otamendi. Leandro Paredes was shown a red card after punching Gavi, who had run onto the pitch to celebrate Spain's victory.Ayala also became involved in the incident.Television footage showed the former Argentina defender approaching Dani Olmo before making contact with the Spain midfielder. Olmo chose not to retaliate.Speaking after the incident, Ayala admitted he had made a mistake and said he regretted losing control."Obviously I'm sorry. Because of my position, I can't allow a feeling, or what I might receive from the other party, to change my mood and my actions.I'm sorry, but for me, these are things that stay there and that's it," Ayala said in an interview with Valencia Capital Radio."For me, things need to be put behind us and left there. It was more of a push than anything else, it wasn't a punch like they're saying, and that's it. It was a reaction to something he said, but that's it. If I see him, I'll obviously apologise to him in person," he said.Ayala said emotions got the better of him during the chaotic scenes and accepted full responsibility for his behaviour."It's a shame, and you have to accept the facts and the things you've done on the field. When the game ends, what I see is a fight in the middle of the pitch, and we rush to go after our players, and it ends up like that because that's not who we are," he said.He added that his original intention was to stop the confrontation rather than become part of it."I take responsibility for what I did. My intention was to go and separate them, that was my intention, but sometimes things happen and emotions run high, but that's no excuse. And given my position, my behaviour has to be different, regardless of what I receive," he said.FIFA has opened disciplinary proceedings into the post-match brawl.The governing body's disciplinary committee has appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to investigate the incidents involving players and coaching staff.
Article Summary: Argentina assistant coach Roberto Ayala apologises for altercation with Spain midfielder Dani Olmo. The ugly scenes unfolded after Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 in extra time on Sunday to lift the World Cup title. Ayala said emotions got the better of him during the chaotic scenes and accepted full responsibility for his behaviour.

Article Title: What does Aaron Rodgers' "#fam" Instagram caption really mean after years of refusing to speak to his own family?
Article Text:
Aaron Rodgers' family (Getty Images)

How did Aaron Rodgers' family feud start in the first place?

What led to Aaron Rodgers' 2026 reunion with his family?

Aaron Rodgers posted five Instagram photos on July 20 that quietly said everything words could not. There he was, arm around his mom Darla, standing beside his dad Ed, helping brother Luke assemble a toy, and playing uncle to two young kids. He captioned it simply: "Another bonding week. #fam." For a man who spent nearly a decade cut off from his own family, that caption landed like a full confession. What fans did not know at the time was that the reconciliation had already been underway for months, well before the Instagram post made it public.The exact origins of the falling out remain unclear, but the breakdown traces back to late 2014, around the time Aaron Rodgers began dating actress Olivia Munn . According to author Ian O'Connor's book, Munn allegedly called Ed and Darla Rodgers after a tough loss against the Buffalo Bills and blindsided them with an angry rant about attending an upcoming game. Ed's response was blunt: "You haven't been on the scene very long. You're just his girlfriend. We're his parents." That phone call is widely considered the moment things cracked beyond repair, at least for a while.The feud stayed private until 2016, when it exploded into public view. Jordan Rodgers joined JoJo Fletcher's season of The Bachelorette and, during his hometown date, told her plainly: "I have a great relationship with my brother Luke.Me and Aaron don't really have that much of a relationship. It's just kind of the way he's chosen to do life." Production underlined the point by placing two empty chairs at the dinner table to mark Aaron's absence, and with it, Olivia Munn's. Millions of football fans who had never thought much about Rodgers' personal life suddenly had an opinion.Religion played a role too. In his 2024 Netflix documentary, Rodgers spoke candidly about growing up in what he described as a "very white, dogmatic church" that felt rigid and guilt-driven. "Shame, guilt, judgment," he said. "Our way is heaven, your way is hell." He said he had begun pulling away from that framework in high school, and even talking to his parents about it felt like a dead end.The years that followed were largely silent. Ed Rodgers confirmed to The New York Times in 2017 that Aaron had not spoken to the family since the end of 2014. Aaron skipped Jordan's 2022 wedding to JoJo Fletcher. Jordan, in turn, was reportedly not invited to Aaron's private ceremony with his wife Brittani.When the Netflix documentary dropped in late 2024, Rodgers finally addressed the Bachelorette episode directly. His frustration was unfiltered. "I was quiet about it, because I thought the best way to do it was not to talk about it publicly," Rodgers said. "And what do they do? They go on a bullshit show and leave two empty chairs?"The thaw began slowly, well away from the cameras. In July 2023, Ed Rodgers made the trip to Lake Tahoe to watch his son play in the American Century Championship golf tournament. Aaron did not know his father was coming. When he spotted him in the crowd, he decided it was time to break the ice, and the two spent time together. Both parents then attended Aaron's first game as a New York Jet that September. Small steps. Nothing announced.TMZ obtained footage from April 2026 showing Rodgers laughing and chatting with Ed and Darla at a Hall of Fame dinner in Chico, California, where he was inducted into the Pleasant Valley High School Athletics Hall of Fame. He thanked his parents in his speech. By the time the Instagram carousel went live in July, this was not a sudden breakthrough but the public confirmation of something that had been quietly healing for three years.Jordan Rodgers did not appear in the photos, though he liked the post. Luke responded with two red heart emojis. The question of where things stand between Aaron and Jordan remains open. But heading into what Rodgers has confirmed will be his final NFL season with the Pittsburgh Steelers, he appears to have made peace with at least part of what he left behind.
Article Summary: Aaron Rodgers posted five Instagram photos on July 20 that quietly said everything words could not. The breakdown traces back to late 2014, around the time Aaron Rodgers began dating actress Olivia Munn. Ed Rodgers confirmed to The New York Times in 2017 that Aaron had not spoken to the family since the end of 2014.

Article Title: "There’s a difference between being a VIP and being Taylor Swift’s VIP": Blake Lively is reportedly no longer getting the celebrity treatment that came with being Taylor Swift's best friend
Article Text: "There’s a difference between being a VIP and being Taylor Swift’s VIP": Blake Lively is reportedly no longer getting the celebrity treatment that came with being Taylor Swift's best friend
Article Summary: Blake Lively is reportedly no longer getting the celebrity treatment that came with being Taylor Swift's best friend. "There’s a difference between being a VIP and being Taylor's VIP," a source told CNN. Lively and Swift have been friends for years.
